# The Tower

Houraisan Kaguya is a NEET princess who loves to watch videos at home. Recently, she often watches videos on a famous video-sharing website called Mikufans.

There is a useful feature on Mikufans that allows users to leave a message during the video playback, which is called danmaku. Sometimes, there are so many danmaku messages at the same time that Kaguya cannot take them all in.

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/14c5f1e145d1b962165119831d2f7a84f4f04bc4.png) Source: [https://bilibili.com/video/BV1xx411c79H](https://bilibili.com/video/BV1xx411c79H)

For simplicity, we only focus on the top danmaku messages: top danmaku messages are displayed at the top of the video screen, and each message occupies exactly one line. There is no limit to the number of danmaku messages at the same time (although Kaguya's screen will only display the first $$$10^9$$$ lines, the remaining messages will still be correctly maintained in the overflow area of the screen).

During the video playback, there may be three types of events:

- A new user sends some top danmaku messages. Each message will be placed at the topmost empty line in order.

- The danmaku messages from a specific user disappear, and the lines they are in become empty lines. The other messages will not be affected and still remain in their positions.

- Kaguya is interested in a danmaku message, so she wants to know the sender of the top danmaku message at a specific line.

Kaguya has many videos to watch every day, and she is too busy to re-watch the video from the beginning, so she asks you for help. Please help her find the senders of the danmaku messages.

## Input

The first line of input contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 5 \times 10^5$$$), representing the number of events.

Each of the following $$$n$$$ lines contains one event in order. Each event is described in one of the following formats:

- `1 k`: A new user sends $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \le k \le 10^9$$$) top danmaku messages. The ID of the user is the smallest positive integer that has not been used before.

- `2 u`: The danmaku messages from user $$$u$$$ disappeared. It is guaranteed that the ID is valid, and the danmaku messages from user $$$u$$$ have not disappeared before.

- `3 l`: Kaguya wants to know the ID of the sender of the danmaku message at the $$$l$$$-th ($$$1 \le l \le 10^9$$$) topmost line. If that line is empty, the answer is defined as `0`.

## Output

For each query of type `3`, output the answer in a single line.

# ## 题目

Tower

Houraisan Kaguya 是一位喜欢在家看视频的 NEET 公主。最近，她经常在一个名为 Mikufans 的著名视频分享网站上观看视频。

Mikufans 上有一个实用的功能，允许用户在视频播放期间留言，这被称为弹幕。有时，同一时间有太多弹幕消息，Kaguya 无法全部接收。

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/14c5f1e145d1b962165119831d2f7a84f4f04bc4.png) 来源：[https://bilibili.com/video/BV1xx411c79H](https://bilibili.com/video/BV1xx411c79H)

为简单起见，我们只关注顶部弹幕：顶部弹幕显示在视频屏幕的顶部，每条消息恰好占据一行。同一时间的弹幕消息数量没有限制（尽管 Kaguya 的屏幕只会显示前 $$$10^9$$$ 行，剩余的消息仍会正确保存在屏幕的溢出区域中）。

在视频播放期间，可能会有三种类型的事件：

- 一个新用户发送一些顶部弹幕消息。每条消息将按顺序放置在顶部最靠上的空行中。

- 某个特定用户的弹幕消息消失，它们所在的行变为空行。其他消息不会受到影响，仍保持在它们的位置上。

- Kaguya 对某条弹幕消息感兴趣，所以她想在特定行知道顶部弹幕消息的发送者。

Kaguya 每天有很多视频要看，她太忙了，无法从头重新观看视频，所以她向你求助。请帮助她找到弹幕消息的发送者。

## 输入

输入的第一行包含一个整数 $$$n$$$（$$$1 \le n \le 5 \times 10^5$$$），表示事件的数量。

接下来的 $$$n$$$ 行按顺序每行包含一个事件。每个事件以下列格式之一描述：

- `1 k`：一个新用户发送 $$$k$$$（$$$1 \le k \le 10^9$$$）条顶部弹幕消息。该用户的 ID 是之前未使用过的最小正整数。

- `2 u`：用户 $$$u$$$ 的弹幕消息消失了。保证该 ID 有效，并且用户 $$$u$$$ 的弹幕消息之前没有消失过。

- `3 l`：Kaguya 想知道第 $$$l$$$（$$$1 \le l \le 10^9$$$）条最顶部行上的弹幕消息发送者的 ID。如果该行为空，答案定义为 `0`。

## 输出

对于每个类型为 `3` 的查询，在一行中输出答案。

# Judgement

On a weekend, Qingshan and her friend Daniel created a one-player game called Generalissimos, in which players can draw great paintings.

The game is played on an $$$n\times m$$$ table. A cell has its color, which is one of red, blue, or white. Initially, cell $$$(a,b)$$$ is red, cell $$$(c,d)$$$ is blue (These two cells do not coincide), and others are white. We call $$$(a,b)$$$ and $$$(c,d)$$$ special cells and others nonspecial. During the game, the player can perform a certain operation, which consists of three steps:

- The player selects a nonspecial cell $$$(x, y)$$$.

- The player selects another cell $$$(x', y')$$$. It must be non-white, and it must be neighboring to $$$(x, y)$$$ (i.e., $$$(x', y')$$$ and $$$(x, y)$$$ must have a common edge).

- The cell $$$(x, y)$$$ is painted with the color of the cell $$$(x', y')$$$.

In other words, in one operation, the player can color a nonspecial cell with the same color as its non-white neighboring cell. Note that a cell may be colored more than once, and the latest color will cover the earlier one.

The player can perform the operation any number of times and then stop the game. After that, the final configuration of the map table is printed.

Unfortunately, Generalissimo is full of cheats, and cheaters can color in any position at any time. In order to advocate Justice, you decide to write a judge program to determine whether the given configuration is possible to be a legal configuration in a normal game, or there must be a cheater.

## Input

The input consists of multiple test cases. The first line contains a single integer $$$T$$$ ($$$1\le T\le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows.

The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le n,m \le 500$$$ and $$$2 \le n\cdot m$$$) — the number of rows and columns.

The second line contains four integers $$$a$$$, $$$b$$$, $$$c$$$, and $$$d$$$ ($$$1 \le a,c \le n$$$ and $$$1 \le b,d \le m$$$).

Each of the next $$$n$$$ lines contains $$$m$$$ characters. Each character is '`R`', '`B`', or '`.`', representing a red cell, a blue cell, and a white cell, respectively.

It is guaranteed that cell $$$(a,b)$$$ and $$$(c,d)$$$ do not coincide, and that the character on the $$$a$$$-th row $$$b$$$-th column and $$$c$$$-th row $$$d$$$-th column is '`R`' and '`B`', respectively.

It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n \cdot m$$$ among $$$T$$$ test cases does not exceed $$$250\,000$$$.

## Output

For each test case, print "`YES`" (without quotes) if it is a legal configuration and "`NO`" (without quotes) otherwise.

You can print letters in any case (upper or lower).

## Note

The following graph shows the first test case and how the player can reach the configuration without cheating. Each crown marks a special cell.

# 判定

在一个周末，青山和她的朋友 Daniel 创造了一款名为 Generalissimos 的单人游戏，玩家可以在其中绘制伟大的画作。

游戏在一个 $$$n\times m$$$ 的表格上进行。每个格子有一种颜色，为红色、蓝色或白色之一。初始时，格子 $$$(a,b)$$$ 是红色，格子 $$$(c,d)$$$ 是蓝色（这两个格子不重合），其他格子是白色。我们称 $$$(a,b)$$$ 和 $$$(c,d)$$$ 为特殊格子，其他格子为非特殊格子。在游戏过程中，玩家可以执行某种操作，该操作由三个步骤组成：

- 玩家选择一个非特殊格子 $$$(x, y)$$$。

- 玩家选择另一个格子 $$$(x', y')$$$。它必须是非白色的，并且必须与 $$$(x, y)$$$ 相邻（即 $$$(x', y')$$$ 和 $$$(x, y)$$$ 必须有一条公共边）。

- 单元格 $$$(x, y)$$$ 被涂成单元格 $$$(x', y')$$$ 的颜色。

换句话说，在一次操作中，玩家可以将一个非特殊格子染成与其非白色相邻格子相同的颜色。注意，一个格子可能被染色多次，最新的颜色会覆盖之前的颜色。

玩家可以执行任意次操作，然后停止游戏。之后，打印地图表的最终配置。

不幸的是，Generalissimo 充满了作弊者，而作弊者可以在任意时刻给任意位置染色。为了倡导正义，你决定编写一个裁判程序，来判断给定的局面是否可能是一场正常游戏中的合法局面，还是必定存在作弊者。

## 输入

输入包含多个测试用例。第一行包含一个整数 $$$T$$$（$$$1\le T\le 10^4$$$）——测试用例的数量。测试用例的描述如下。

第一行包含两个整数 $$$n$$$、$$$m$$$（$$$1 \le n,m \le 500$$$ 且 $$$2 \le n\cdot m$$$）——行数和列数。

第二行包含四个整数 $$$a$$$、$$$b$$$、$$$c$$$ 和 $$$d$$$（$$$1 \le a,c \le n$$$ 且 $$$1 \le b,d \le m$$$）。

接下来的 $$$n$$$ 行中，每行包含 $$$m$$$ 个字符。每个字符是 '`R`'、'`B`' 或 '`.`'，分别表示红色格子、蓝色格子和白色格子。

保证格子 $$$(a,b)$$$ 和 $$$(c,d)$$$ 不重合，且第 $$$a$$$ 行第 $$$b$$$ 列和第 $$$c$$$ 行第 $$$d$$$ 列上的字符分别为 '`R`' 和 '`B`'。

保证在 $$$T$$$ 个测试用例中，$$$n \cdot m$$$ 的总和不超过 $$$250\,000$$$。

## 输出

对于每个测试用例，如果它是合法配置，则输出 "`YES`"（不带引号），否则输出 "`NO`"（不带引号）。

字母可以以任意大小写（大写或小写）输出。

## 提示

下图展示了第一个测试用例以及玩家如何在不作弊的情况下达到该配置。每个皇冠标记一个特殊格子。

# Safety First

A ladder has $$$n$$$ sections, each of which has a positive integer length, and the lengths are sequentially non-increasing. That is, the lengths of these $$$n$$$ sections from left to right $$$d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_n$$$ should satisfy $$$d_1 \ge d_2 \ge \cdots \ge d_n$$$.

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/12a8bb777e5760897f8054f04a7fcd362231f97f.png)

Little Q needs a ladder that, when stood upright, has a height exactly equal to $$$m$$$, where the height of a ladder is defined as the altitude difference between its highest end and its lowest end. For safety reasons, this ladder needs to be stable, which means it satisfies the following requirements:

- The lower end of the first section of the ladder must touch the ground;

- For each $$$i=1,2,\ldots,n-1$$$, the upper end of the $$$i$$$-th section must be locked into either the upper end or the lower end of the $$$(i+1)$$$-th section.

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8986aedcfc8bd2b5e7cfc7b61f6bdeb4d921d951.png)

You need to compute the number of different stable ladders with $$$n$$$ sections that can be constructed if their height when stood upright is exactly $$$m$$$. Two ladders are considered different if and only if there exists some $$$k$$$ such that the lengths of the $$$k$$$-th section of the two ladders are different, or if the $$$k$$$-th section of one ladder is locked into the upper end of the $$$(k+1)$$$-th section while the $$$k$$$-th section of the other ladder is locked into the lower end of the $$$(k+1)$$$-th section.

Since the answer may be large, output it modulo $$$998\,244\,353$$$.

## Input

The first line of the input contains an integer $$$T$$$ ($$$1 \le T \le 10^5$$$), indicating the number of test cases. For each test case:

The only line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le n, m \le 2\,000$$$), indicating the number of sections and the required height of the stable ladder.

## Output

For each test case, output a line containing an integer, indicating the number of different stable ladders modulo $$$998\,244\,353$$$.

## Note

In the following explanation, we use bold text to indicate that the upper end of the corresponding section is locked into the lower bound of the next section and keep the same in other scenarios.

In the first sample case:

- for the first test case, the only possible ladder has a single section of length $$$1$$$;

- for the second test case, the section lengths of all $$$4$$$ possible ladders are $$$[\textbf{2}, 1]$$$, $$$[3, 1]$$$, $$$[3, 2]$$$ and $$$[3, 3]$$$ respectively;

- for the third test case, the section lengths of all $$$10$$$ possible ladders are $$$[\textbf{1}, \textbf{1}, 1]$$$, $$$[\textbf{2}, 1, 1]$$$, $$$[2, \textbf{1}, 1]$$$, $$$[2, \textbf{2}, 1]$$$, $$$[3, 1, 1]$$$, $$$[3, 2, 1]$$$, $$$[3, 2, 2]$$$, $$$[3, 3, 1]$$$, $$$[3, 3, 2]$$$ and $$$[3, 3, 3]$$$ respectively.

# 安全第一

一个梯子有 $$$n$$$ 个节段，每个节段都有一个正整数长度，并且这些长度依次非递增。也就是说，这 $$$n$$$ 个节段从左到右的长度 $$$d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_n$$$ 应满足 $$$d_1 \ge d_2 \ge \cdots \ge d_n$$$。

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/12a8bb777e5760897f8054f04a7fcd362231f97f.png)

小 Q 需要一个梯子，当它竖直放置时，高度恰好等于 $$$m$$$，其中梯子的高度定义为其最高端与最低端之间的高度差。出于安全考虑，这个梯子需要是稳定的，这意味着它满足以下要求：

- 梯子第一节段的下端必须接触地面；

- 对于每个 $$$i=1,2,\ldots,n-1$$$，第 $$$i$$$ 个节段的上端必须锁定在第 $$$(i+1)$$$ 个节段的上端或下端。

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8986aedcfc8bd2b5e7cfc7b61f6bdeb4d921d951.png)

你需要计算，如果竖直放置时高度恰好为 $$$m$$$，可以构造出多少个不同的、具有 $$$n$$$ 个节段的稳定梯子。两个梯子被认为是不同的，当且仅当存在某个 $$$k$$$，使得两个梯子第 $$$k$$$ 个节段的长度不同，或者一个梯子的第 $$$k$$$ 个节段锁定在第 $$$(k+1)$$$ 个节段的上端，而另一个梯子的第 $$$k$$$ 个节段锁定在第 $$$(k+1)$$$ 个节段的下端。

由于答案可能很大，请将其对 $$$998\,244\,353$$$ 取模后输出。

## 输入

输入的第一行包含一个整数 $$$T$$$（$$$1 \le T \le 10^5$$$），表示测试用例的数量。对于每个测试用例：

唯一一行包含两个整数 $$$n$$$ 和 $$$m$$$（$$$1 \le n, m \le 2\,000$$$），分别表示节段数量和稳定梯子所需的高度。

## 输出

对于每个测试用例，输出一行一个整数，表示不同稳定梯子的数量对 $$$998\,244\,353$$$ 取模后的结果。

## 提示

在下面的解释中，我们使用粗体文本表示相应节段的上端锁定在下一节段的下端，并在其他情形中保持一致。

在第一个样例中：

- 对于第一个测试用例，唯一可能的梯子只有一个长度为 $$$1$$$ 的节段；

- 对于第二个测试用例，所有 $$$4$$$ 个可能梯子的节段长度分别为 $$$[\textbf{2}, 1]$$$、$$$[3, 1]$$$、$$$[3, 2]$$$ 和 $$$[3, 3]$$$；

- 对于第三个测试用例，所有 $$$10$$$ 种可能的梯子的段长分别为 $$$[\textbf{1}, \textbf{1}, 1]$$$、$$$[\textbf{2}, 1, 1]$$$、$$$[2, \textbf{1}, 1]$$$、$$$[2, \textbf{2}, 1]$$$、$$$[3, 1, 1]$$$、$$$[3, 2, 1]$$$、$$$[3, 2, 2]$$$、$$$[3, 3, 1]$$$、$$$[3, 3, 2]$$$ 和 $$$[3, 3, 3]$$$。

# Crisis Event: Meteorite

Sulfox the fennec fox has recently become obsessed with Anomaly Collapse, a roguelite turn-based strategy game built around its innovative one-dimensional battlefield grid system. As he controls his squad of warriors to fight against enemies on the special battlefield, where positioning mechanisms and proper allocation of ability points are crucial for victory, he encounters another crisis event (a thoughtful "gift" from the game designers) as the factor introduced to escalate the challenge of the new chapter — Meteorite.



For this problem, let's push this crisis event to a more extreme version than the original game. Consider a linear battlefield consisting of $$$n$$$ grids numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ sequentially. Initially, the battlefield is clear of any meteorites, and several characters are positioned on certain grids. Sulfox's objective is to ensure the survival of all characters through $$$m$$$ rounds of the meteorite disaster.



At the beginning of the $$$i$$$-th round ($$$i = 1, 2, \ldots, m$$$), the fatal meteorite hazard unfolds: For each $$$j = 1, 2, \ldots, n$$$, exactly $$$a_{i,j}$$$ (possibly zero) meteorites descend upon the $$$j$$$-th grid, accumulating with any existing meteorites. Movement of characters is prohibited during this phase, which means any character unfortunate enough to be standing on a grid where meteorites descend will instantly be squashed into a pancake.

 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c7ca284fd55e0dd639dad15a798edf0d6383d79b.png) Do not let character stand on the grid where meteorites descend 

The action phase occurs after all meteorites for the $$$i$$$-th round have landed, during which Sulfox can move any surviving character to an adjacent grid, and this movement may be performed arbitrarily many times (possibly zero) for each character before this round ends. However, existing meteorites block characters from entering their occupied grids. Therefore, before a character can enter such a grid, Sulfox must spend $$$1$$$ point per meteorite on that grid to destroy them.



Please help Sulfox calculate the minimum number of points required to ensure the survival of all characters throughout the meteorite disaster, or report that it is an impossible mission to achieve the objective.



## Input



The first line of the input contains an integer $$$T$$$ ($$$1 \le T \le 10^4$$$), indicating the number of test cases. For each test case:



The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \leq n, m \leq 10^6$$$, $$$1 \leq n \times m \leq 10^6$$$), indicating the number of grids and the number of rounds respectively.



The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$c_1, c_2, \ldots, c_n$$$ ($$$c_i \in \{0, 1\}$$$). There is a character positioned on the $$$i$$$-th grid initially if and only if $$$c_i = 1$$$. It is guaranteed that there is at least one character in the game.



Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, the $$$i$$$-th of which contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_{i, 1}, a_{i, 2}, \ldots, a_{i, n}$$$ ($$$0 \leq a_{i, j} \leq 1\,000$$$), indicating that $$$a_{i, j}$$$ meteorites descend upon the $$$j$$$-th grid at the beginning of the $$$i$$$-th round.



It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n \times m$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^6$$$.



## Output



For each test case, if it is impossible to ensure the survival of all characters, output $$$-1$$$ in one line. Otherwise, output an integer in one line, indicating the minimum number of points required.

# 危机事件：陨石

耳廓狐Sulfox最近迷上了《异常坍缩》，这是一款以创新的“一维战场网格系统”为核心的Roguelite回合制策略游戏。当他操控自己的战士小队，在特殊战场上与敌人作战时——在这片战场上，站位机制与能力点的合理分配对胜利至关重要——他遭遇了另一个危机事件（游戏设计者精心准备的“礼物”），也就是为提升新章节挑战性而引入的因素——陨石。



对于本题，让我们把这个危机事件推到比原游戏更极端的版本。考虑一个由$$$n$$$个网格依次编号为$$$1$$$到$$$n$$$的线性战场。初始时，战场上没有任何陨石，若干角色位于某些网格上。Sulfox的目标是确保所有角色在$$$m$$$轮陨石灾难中全部存活。



在第$$$i$$$轮开始时（$$$i = 1, 2, \ldots, m$$$），致命的陨石灾害发生：对于每个$$$j = 1, 2, \ldots, n$$$，恰好有$$$a_{i,j}$$$（可能为零）颗陨石降落到第$$$j$$$个网格上，并与已有的陨石累积。此阶段禁止角色移动，这意味着任何不幸站在有陨石降落的网格上的角色都会立刻被压成薄饼。

 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c7ca284fd55e0dd639dad15a798edf0d6383d79b.png) 不要让角色站在有陨石降落的网格上 

行动阶段发生在第$$$i$$$轮的所有陨石落地之后，在此期间Sulfox可以将任何存活角色移动到相邻网格，并且在本轮结束前，每个角色都可以任意多次（可能为零次）执行此移动。然而，已有的陨石会阻挡角色进入其占据的网格。因此，在角色能够进入这样的网格之前，Sulfox必须为那个网格上的每颗陨石花费$$$1$$$点来摧毁它们。



请帮助Sulfox计算确保所有角色在整个陨石灾难中存活所需的最少点数，或者报告该目标是不可能完成的任务。



## 输入



输入的第一行包含一个整数$$$T$$$（$$$1 \le T \le 10^4$$$），表示测试用例的数量。对于每个测试用例：



第一行包含两个整数$$$n$$$和$$$m$$$（$$$1 \leq n, m \leq 10^6$$$，$$$1 \leq n \times m \leq 10^6$$$），分别表示网格数量和回合数量。



第二行包含$$$n$$$个整数$$$c_1, c_2, \ldots, c_n$$$（$$$c_i \in \{0, 1\}$$$）。当且仅当$$$c_i = 1$$$时，第$$$i$$$个网格初始时有一个角色。保证游戏中至少有一个角色。



接下来有 $$$m$$$ 行，其中第 $$$i$$$ 行包含 $$$n$$$ 个整数 $$$a_{i, 1}, a_{i, 2}, \ldots, a_{i, n}$$$（$$$0 \leq a_{i, j} \leq 1\,000$$$），表示在第 $$$i$$$ 轮开始时，有 $$$a_{i, j}$$$ 颗陨石降落在第 $$$j$$$ 个格子上。



保证所有测试用例中 $$$n \times m$$$ 的总和不超过 $$$10^6$$$。



## 输出



对于每个测试用例，如果无法保证所有角色的存活，则在一行中输出 $$$-1$$$。否则，在一行中输出一个整数，表示所需的最少点数。

# Dot Product Game

A permutation of $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ in this problem is a $$$1$$$-based sequence of $$$n$$$ integers in which every integer from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ appears exactly once. Alice and Bob are playing a game on $$$A = [a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n]$$$ and $$$B = [b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n]$$$, two permutations of $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. They take turns to perform operations, with Alice going first, and the one with no possible operation loses.



In each turn, Alice can only operate on the permutation $$$A$$$, while Bob can only operate on the permutation $$$B$$$. A valid operation consists of choosing two indices $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$ on the operable permutation ($$$1 \leq i, j \leq n$$$) and swapping their corresponding elements, under the constraint that $$$\sum_{i=1}^{n}{a_i b_i} = a_1 b_1 + a_2 b_2 + \cdots + a_n b_n$$$, the dot product of these two permutations, must strictly increase after the swap. Namely, a player loses if he or she cannot perform any swap to increase the dot product, and the other player wins the game.



As Alice and Bob are both clever enough to adopt the best strategy, the winner of such a game can be determined from the start. Therefore, they decide to play the game $$$n$$$ times with modifications to make it less boring. Please help them to predict the winners of these $$$n$$$ games.



More specifically, two initial permutations $$$A = [a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n]$$$, $$$B = [b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n]$$$, and $$$(n - 1)$$$ modifications $$$[(t_1, l_1, r_1, d_1), (t_2, l_2, r_2, d_2), \ldots, (t_{n - 1}, l_{n - 1}, r_{n - 1}, d_{n - 1})]$$$ will be given. The first game will start from the given permutations $$$A$$$ and $$$B$$$, and for $$$k = 1, 2, \ldots, n - 1$$$, the $$$(k + 1)$$$-th game will start from the permutations for the $$$k$$$-th game after shifting the interval between indices $$$l_k$$$ and $$$r_k$$$ of the permutation $$$t_k$$$ left $$$d_k$$$ times.



Please note that shifting an interval $$$[p_l, p_{l + 1}, \ldots, p_r]$$$ left once will give $$$[p_{l + 1}, p_{l + 2}, \ldots, p_r, p_l]$$$. For instance, shifting the interval $$$[2, 4]$$$ of $$$[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]$$$ left once will give $$$[1, 3, 4, 2, 5]$$$, and twice will give $$$[1, 4, 2, 3, 5]$$$. Besides, shifting the interval $$$[1, 5]$$$ of $$$[3, 1, 4, 5, 2]$$$ left $$$4$$$ times will give $$$[2, 3, 1, 4, 5]$$$.



## Input



The first line of the input contains an integer $$$T$$$ ($$$1 \leq T \leq 10^5$$$), indicating the number of test cases. For each test case:



The first line contains an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 5 \times 10^5$$$), indicating the length of the permutations.



The second line contains $$$n$$$ distinct integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_i \leq n$$$), indicating the permutation $$$A$$$.



The third line contains $$$n$$$ distinct integers $$$b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq b_i \leq n$$$), indicating the permutation $$$B$$$.



In the next $$$(n - 1)$$$ lines, the $$$i$$$-th line contains a character $$$t_i$$$ ($$$t_i \in \{\texttt{A}, \texttt{B}\}$$$), and three integers $$$l_i$$$, $$$r_i$$$ ($$$1 \leq l_i \leq r_i \leq n$$$), and $$$d_i$$$ ($$$1 \leq d_i \leq n$$$).



It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$5 \times 10^5$$$.



## Output



For each test case, output a string of length $$$n$$$ in one line, where the $$$i$$$-th character of the string is `A` if Alice wins the $$$i$$$-th game, or `B` otherwise (i.e., Bob wins the $$$i$$$-th game).



## Note



For the third test case of the sample case:



- The first game starts with $$$A = [1, 2, 3]$$$, $$$B = [2, 1, 3]$$$;

- The second game starts with $$$A = [2, 3, 1]$$$, $$$B = [2, 1, 3]$$$;

- The third game starts with $$$A = [2, 3, 1]$$$, $$$B = [1, 2, 3]$$$.

# 点积游戏

本题中，$$$1$$$ 到 $$$n$$$ 的一个排列是一个基于 $$$1$$$ 的、由 $$$n$$$ 个整数组成的序列，其中从 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$n$$$ 的每个整数恰好出现一次。Alice 和 Bob 正在 $$$A = [a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n]$$$ 和 $$$B = [b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n]$$$ 这两个 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$n$$$ 的排列上玩游戏。他们轮流执行操作，Alice 先手，无法执行操作者输。



在每一回合中，Alice 只能对排列 $$$A$$$ 进行操作，而 Bob 只能对排列 $$$B$$$ 进行操作。一次合法操作包括在可操作的排列上选择两个下标 $$$i$$$ 和 $$$j$$$（$$$1 \leq i, j \leq n$$$）并交换它们对应的元素，约束条件是交换后 $$$\sum_{i=1}^{n}{a_i b_i} = a_1 b_1 + a_2 b_2 + \cdots + a_n b_n$$$，即这两个排列的点积，必须严格增大。也就是说，如果一名玩家无法执行任何使点积增大的交换，则该玩家输，另一名玩家赢得游戏。



由于 Alice 和 Bob 都足够聪明，会采取最优策略，因此这样一场游戏的胜者从一开始就可以确定。于是，他们决定将游戏进行 $$$n$$$ 次并加以修改，以免过于无聊。请帮助他们预测这 $$$n$$$ 场游戏的胜者。



更具体地说，会给出两个初始排列 $$$A = [a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n]$$$、$$$B = [b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n]$$$，以及 $$$(n - 1)$$$ 次修改 $$$[(t_1, l_1, r_1, d_1), (t_2, l_2, r_2, d_2), \ldots, (t_{n - 1}, l_{n - 1}, r_{n - 1}, d_{n - 1})]$$$。第一场游戏将从给定的排列 $$$A$$$ 和 $$$B$$$ 开始；对于 $$$k = 1, 2, \ldots, n - 1$$$，第 $$$(k + 1)$$$ 场游戏将从第 $$$k$$$ 场游戏的排列开始，但需先将排列 $$$t_k$$$ 中下标 $$$l_k$$$ 到 $$$r_k$$$ 之间的区间向左移动 $$$d_k$$$ 次。



请注意，将区间 $$$[p_l, p_{l + 1}, \ldots, p_r]$$$ 向左移动一次将得到 $$$[p_{l + 1}, p_{l + 2}, \ldots, p_r, p_l]$$$。例如，将 $$$[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]$$$ 的区间 $$$[2, 4]$$$ 向左移动一次将得到 $$$[1, 3, 4, 2, 5]$$$，移动两次将得到 $$$[1, 4, 2, 3, 5]$$$。此外，将 $$$[3, 1, 4, 5, 2]$$$ 的区间 $$$[1, 5]$$$ 向左移动 $$$4$$$ 次将得到 $$$[2, 3, 1, 4, 5]$$$。



## 输入



输入的第一行包含一个整数 $$$T$$$（$$$1 \leq T \leq 10^5$$$），表示测试用例的数量。对于每个测试用例：



第一行包含一个整数 $$$n$$$（$$$1 \leq n \leq 5 \times 10^5$$$），表示排列的长度。



第二行包含 $$$n$$$ 个互不相同的整数 $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$（$$$1 \leq a_i \leq n$$$），表示排列 $$$A$$$。



第三行包含 $$$n$$$ 个互不相同的整数 $$$b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n$$$（$$$1 \leq b_i \leq n$$$），表示排列 $$$B$$$。



在接下来的 $$$(n - 1)$$$ 行中，第 $$$i$$$ 行包含一个字符 $$$t_i$$$（$$$t_i \in \{\texttt{A}, \texttt{B}\}$$$），以及三个整数 $$$l_i$$$、$$$r_i$$$（$$$1 \leq l_i \leq r_i \leq n$$$）和 $$$d_i$$$（$$$1 \leq d_i \leq n$$$）。



保证所有测试用例中 $$$n$$$ 的总和不超过 $$$5 \times 10^5$$$。



## 输出



对于每个测试用例，在一行中输出一个长度为 $$$n$$$ 的字符串，其中字符串的第 $$$i$$$ 个字符为 `A` 表示 Alice 赢得第 $$$i$$$ 局游戏，否则为 `B`（即 Bob 赢得第 $$$i$$$ 局游戏）。



## 提示



对于样例中的第三个测试用例：



- 第一局游戏开始时 $$$A = [1, 2, 3]$$$、$$$B = [2, 1, 3]$$$；

- 第二局游戏开始时 $$$A = [2, 3, 1]$$$、$$$B = [2, 1, 3]$$$；

- 第三局游戏开始时 $$$A = [2, 3, 1]$$$、$$$B = [1, 2, 3]$$$。

# Light Up the Grid

Little Q is testing a self-designed puzzle game involving a $$$2 \times 2$$$ grid where each cell can either be on or off. When a cell is toggled, its state changes from off to on or from on to off. The following four operations can be performed at a certain cost:



- Toggle a single cell with cost $$$a_0$$$;

- Toggle a row of cells with cost $$$a_1$$$;

- Toggle a column of cells with cost $$$a_2$$$;

- Toggle all cells with cost $$$a_3$$$.



Little Q has realized that the game has started, but the screen somehow malfunctions, blocking him from seeing the current state of any cell. The only feedback he can receive is a special prompt sound triggered if, after an operation, all cells are on.



Knowing all $$$m$$$ possible initial grids of the game in advance, Little Q wants to find a sequence of operations, ensuring that regardless of the initial grid when he starts playing, he will always hear the prompt sound after some operations in the order of the sequence.



Please calculate the minimum total cost of such sequence of operations.



## Input



The first line of the input contains five integers $$$T$$$ ($$$1 \le T \le 10^4$$$), $$$a_0$$$, $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, and $$$a_3$$$ ($$$1 \le a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3 \le 10^6$$$), indicating the number of games and the costs of each operation. For each game:



The first line contains an integer $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le m \le 16$$$), indicating the number of possible initial grids of the game.



Then $$$m$$$ grids follow. For each grid:



- There will first be an empty line if it is not the first grid in the game.

- For the following two lines, the $$$i$$$-th line contains a string $$$s_{i,1}s_{i,2}$$$ of length $$$2$$$ consisting of characters `0` and `1`, describing a $$$2 \times 2$$$ grid as a possible initial grid. Let $$$(i, j)$$$ be the cell on the $$$i$$$-th row and the $$$j$$$-th column. If $$$s_{i, j}$$$ is `0`, then the cell $$$(i, j)$$$ is off, or otherwise the cell $$$(i, j)$$$ is on.



It is guaranteed that the given grids in a game are pairwise different.



## Output



For each game, output a line containing an integer, indicating the minimum total cost.

# 点亮网格

小 Q 正在测试一个自己设计的谜题游戏，游戏涉及一个 $$$2 \times 2$$$ 的网格，其中每个格子可以处于开启或关闭状态。当一个格子被切换时，它的状态会从关闭变为开启，或从开启变为关闭。以下四种操作可以以一定的代价执行：



- 以代价 $$$a_0$$$ 切换单个格子；

- 以代价 $$$a_1$$$ 切换一行格子；

- 以代价 $$$a_2$$$ 切换一列格子；

- 以代价 $$$a_3$$$ 切换所有格子。



小 Q 意识到游戏已经开始了，但屏幕不知为何发生了故障，使他无法看到任何格子的当前状态。他唯一能得到的反馈是，如果在某次操作之后所有格子都处于开启状态，就会触发一种特殊的提示音。



由于事先知道游戏所有 $$$m$$$ 种可能的初始网格，小 Q 想找到一个操作序列，确保无论他开始游戏时的初始网格是哪一个，他总能在按该序列顺序执行若干次操作后听到提示音。



请计算这样的操作序列的最小总代价。



## 输入



输入的第一行包含五个整数 $$$T$$$（$$$1 \le T \le 10^4$$$）、$$$a_0$$$、$$$a_1$$$、$$$a_2$$$ 和 $$$a_3$$$（$$$1 \le a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3 \le 10^6$$$），分别表示游戏的数量以及每种操作的代价。对于每个游戏：



第一行包含一个整数 $$$m$$$（$$$1 \le m \le 16$$$），表示该游戏可能的初始网格数量。



接下来是 $$$m$$$ 个网格。对于每个网格：



- 如果它不是该游戏中的第一个网格，则首先会有一个空行。

- 对于接下来的两行，第 $$$i$$$ 行包含一个长度为 $$$2$$$ 的字符串 $$$s_{i,1}s_{i,2}$$$，由字符 `0` 和 `1` 组成，描述一个 $$$2 \times 2$$$ 网格作为可能的初始网格。设 $$$(i, j)$$$ 为第 $$$i$$$ 行第 $$$j$$$ 列的格子。如果 $$$s_{i, j}$$$ 为 `0`，则格子 $$$(i, j)$$$ 是关闭的，否则格子 $$$(i, j)$$$ 是开启的。



保证一个游戏中给定的网格两两不同。



## 输出



对于每个游戏，输出一行，包含一个整数，表示最小总代价。

# Light Up the Hypercube

Do androids dream of electric sheep? This topic, posed decades ago, stung with renewed urgency in future world, serving as a bitter reminder where biological minds had almost surrendered their thinking and creativity to artificial intelligence.



One afternoon in 2040, as Sulfox the fennec fox immersed himself in the pleasure of a simple two-dimensional puzzle game designed by Little Q (introduced in Problem E. Light Up The Grid), his solutions caught the attention of his custom AI system. The AI, despite having achieved nearly omnipotent capabilities in these years, failed to empathize with Sulfox's recreational purpose, misinterpreting his joy as a desire for greater challenges. In a display of its superior grasp of higher dimensions, the AI spontaneously provided an $$$n$$$-dimensional puzzle game that only it could truly comprehend.

 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f3f8e39b69b753b69f518f9c6a2370fe6a37bf7e.png) Self-Important Custom AI System 

The enhanced puzzle game involves an $$$n$$$-dimensional hypercube, where each of its edges extends along only one of the $$$n$$$ dimensions, and each of its $$$2^n$$$ vertices is equipped with a light that can either be on or off. When a light is toggled, its state changes from off to on or from on to off.



Different from the simple puzzle game, there are $$$2^n$$$ kinds of toggle operations which can be performed at a certain cost, each numbered by an integer from $$$0$$$ to $$$\left(2^n-1\right)$$$. Specifically, for operation $$$i$$$ ($$$i = 0,1,\ldots,2^n-1$$$):



- The cost of performing such operation equals $$$a_i$$$;

- Let $$$\overline{b_nb_{n-1}\ldots b_1}$$$ be the binary representation of $$$i$$$, where each $$$b_j \in \{0,1\}$$$ ($$$j = 1,2,\ldots,n$$$) denotes the $$$j$$$-th bit of the binary representation from low to high, such operation allows selecting any valid $$$k$$$-face (subcube of dimensionality $$$k$$$) of the hypercube, where $$$k$$$ is the number of $$$b_j = 1$$$ in the binary representation, each $$$b_j = 1$$$ constrains that the $$$k$$$-face selected must extend along the $$$j$$$-th dimension, and each $$$b_j = 0$$$ constrains that the $$$k$$$-face selected must have zero thickness in the $$$j$$$-th dimension. Then, toggle the lights at all vertices of the $$$k$$$-face selected.



For instance, operation $$$0$$$ toggles the light at a single vertex ($$$0$$$-face) with cost $$$a_0$$$, operations $$$2^0, 2^1, \ldots, 2^{n-1}$$$ toggle lights at both endpoints of an edge ($$$1$$$-face) along their corresponding dimensions with cost $$$a_{2^0}, a_{2^1}, \ldots,a_{2^{n-1}}$$$ respectively, and operation $$$\left(2^n-1\right)$$$ toggles all lights with cost $$$a_{2^n-1}$$$.



Sulfox had realized that the game had started, but the screen had been forbidden by the AI, blocking him from seeing the current state of any light. The only feedback he could receive is a special prompt sound triggered if, after an operation, all lights were on.



Therefore, he needed to find a sequence of operations, ensuring that regardless of the initial state of the lights (among all $$$2^{2^n}$$$ possibilities) when he started playing, he would always hear the prompt sound after some operations in the order of the sequence.



As a three-dimensional being, Sulfox felt impossible to visualize higher dimensions, yet believing the minimum total cost of such sequence of operations was still computable. "OK, AI, I want full manual control now," he said and set about solving, determined to swim free in the pool of cognition rather than be tethered by a lifejacket until forgetting how to stay afloat.



Please calculate the minimum total cost modulo $$$998\,244\,353$$$ since it could be extremely large.



## Input



The first line of the input contains an integer $$$T$$$ ($$$1 \le T \le 10^4$$$), indicating the number of test cases. For each test case:



The first line contains an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 20$$$), indicating the dimensionality of the hypercube.



The second line contains $$$2^n$$$ integers $$$a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_{2^n-1}$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^6$$$), indicating the costs of each operation.



It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$2^n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2^{20}$$$.



## Output



For each test case, output a line containing an integer, indicating the minimum total cost modulo $$$998\,244\,353$$$.

# 点亮超立方体

仿生人会梦见电子羊吗？这个几十年前提出的问题，在未来世界以新的紧迫性再次刺痛人心，苦涩地提醒着人们：生物心智几乎已将思考与创造力拱手让给人工智能。



某天下午，在2040，耳廓狐Sulfox正沉浸在小Q设计的一款简单二维解谜游戏（见问题E. Light Up The Grid）的乐趣中，他的解法引起了他定制AI系统的注意。这个AI尽管在这些年里已近乎无所不能，却无法理解Sulfox的娱乐目的，把他的快乐误认为是对更大挑战的渴望。为了展示自己对更高维度的卓越理解，AI自作主张地提供了一个只有它才能真正理解的$$$n$$$维解谜游戏。

 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f3f8e39b69b753b69f518f9c6a2370fe6a37bf7e.png) 自命不凡的定制AI系统 

这个增强版解谜游戏涉及一个$$$n$$$维超立方体，它的每条棱只沿$$$n$$$个维度之一延伸，它的$$$2^n$$$个顶点各装有一盏可以打开或关闭的灯。当一盏灯被切换时，其状态从关变为开，或从开变为关。



与简单的解谜游戏不同，这里有$$$2^n$$$种切换操作，每种操作都以一定代价执行，编号为从$$$0$$$到$$$\left(2^n-1\right)$$$的整数。具体来说，对于操作$$$i$$$（$$$i = 0,1,\ldots,2^n-1$$$）：



- 执行这种操作的代价等于$$$a_i$$$；

- 设$$$\overline{b_nb_{n-1}\ldots b_1}$$$为$$$i$$$的二进制表示，其中每个$$$b_j \in \{0,1\}$$$（$$$j = 1,2,\ldots,n$$$）表示二进制表示从低到高的第$$$j$$$位，这种操作允许选择超立方体的任意合法$$$k$$$维面（$$$k$$$维子立方体），其中$$$k$$$是二进制表示中$$$b_j = 1$$$的个数，每个$$$b_j = 1$$$约束所选的$$$k$$$维面必须沿第$$$j$$$维延伸，每个$$$b_j = 0$$$约束所选的$$$k$$$维面在第$$$j$$$维上厚度必须为零。然后，切换所选$$$k$$$维面所有顶点处的灯。



例如，操作$$$0$$$以代价$$$a_0$$$切换单个顶点（$$$0$$$维面）处的灯，操作$$$2^0, 2^1, \ldots, 2^{n-1}$$$分别以代价$$$a_{2^0}, a_{2^1}, \ldots,a_{2^{n-1}}$$$切换一条棱（$$$1$$$维面）沿其对应维度两个端点处的灯，而操作$$$\left(2^n-1\right)$$$以代价$$$a_{2^n-1}$$$切换所有灯。



Sulfox 意识到游戏已经开始了，但屏幕被 AI 禁止，使他无法看到任何一盏灯的当前状态。他唯一能得到的反馈是一种特殊的提示音，如果在一次操作之后所有灯都亮着，就会触发该提示音。



因此，他需要找到一个操作序列，确保无论他刚开始游戏时灯的初始状态是什么（在 $$$2^{2^n}$$$ 种可能性之中），按该序列的顺序进行若干次操作后，他总是能听到提示音。



作为一个三维生物，Sulfox 觉得无法将更高维可视化，但他相信这样一个操作序列的最小总代价仍然是可以计算的。“好吧，AI，我现在想要完全手动控制，”他说着便开始求解，决心在认知的海洋中自由游弋，而不是被救生衣拴住，直到忘记如何浮在水面上。



请计算最小总代价对 $$$998\,244\,353$$$ 取模后的结果，因为它可能极其巨大。



## 输入



输入的第一行包含一个整数 $$$T$$$（$$$1 \le T \le 10^4$$$），表示测试用例的数量。对于每个测试用例：



第一行包含一个整数 $$$n$$$（$$$2 \le n \le 20$$$），表示超立方体的维数。



第二行包含 $$$2^n$$$ 个整数 $$$a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_{2^n-1}$$$（$$$1 \le a_i \le 10^6$$$），表示每次操作的代价。



保证所有测试用例中 $$$2^n$$$ 的总和不超过 $$$2^{20}$$$。



## 输出



对于每个测试用例，输出一行一个整数，表示最小总代价对 $$$998\,244\,353$$$ 取模后的结果。

# Guess the Polygon

This is an interactive problem.



You are given a simple polygon, but before giving you the $$$n$$$ vertices of the polygon, Little Q has shuffled them.



Now you can ask Little Q no more than $$$(n-2)$$$ queries, each of which consists of two integers $$$p$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$0 \le p/q \le 1\,000, 1 \le q \le 1\,000$$$). He will tell you the total length of the points on the line $$$x=p/q$$$ that lie inside or on the boundary of the polygon, which can be represented as $$$r/s$$$ with two integers $$$r$$$ and $$$s$$$ ($$$r \ge 0, s \ge 1, \gcd(r,s) = 1$$$). Here $$$\gcd(r,s)$$$ is the greatest common divisor of $$$r$$$ and $$$s$$$.



You need to find the area of the polygon, which can also be represented as $$$u/v$$$ with two integers $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ ($$$u \ge 0, v \ge 1, \gcd(u,v) = 1$$$).



The polygon and the order of the vertices are determined before the start of the interaction and do not depend on your queries. In other words, the interactor is not adaptive.



## Input



The first line of the input contains an integer $$$T$$$ ($$$1 \le T \le 1\,000$$$), indicating the number of test cases. For each test case:



The first line contains an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$3 \le n \le 1\,000$$$), indicating the number of vertices of the polygon.



Then $$$n$$$ lines follow, each containing two integers $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$ ($$$0 \le x,y \le 1\,000$$$) that give the coordinates $$$(x, y)$$$ of the vertices of the polygon in shuffled order.



The polygon is simple, i.e., its vertices are distinct and no two edges of the polygon intersect or touch, except that consecutive edges touch at their common vertex. In addition, no two consecutive edges are collinear.



It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$1\,000$$$.



## Interaction



If you want to ask a query, output one line. First output `?` followed by a space, then output two integers $$$p$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$0 \le p/q \le 1\,000, 1 \le q \le 1\,000$$$). After flushing your output, your program should read two integers $$$r$$$ and $$$s$$$ ($$$r \ge 0, s \ge 1, \gcd(r,s) = 1$$$), indicating the answer to your query.



If you want to guess the area of the polygon, output one line. First output `!` followed by a space, then output two integers $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ ($$$u \ge 0, v \ge 1, \gcd(u,v) = 1$$$), indicating that the area of the polygon is $$$u/v$$$. After flushing your output, your program should continue processing the next test case, or exit immediately if there are no more test cases. Note that your guess does not count as a query.



To flush your output, you can use:



- `fflush(stdout)` (if you use `printf`) or `cout.flush()` (if you use `cout`) in C and C++.

- `System.out.flush()` in Java and Kotlin.

- `sys.stdout.flush()` in Python.



## Note



For the first sample case, there are three candidate polygons, shown in the figure below. Only the leftmost one meets the answer $$$2$$$ to the query $$$x=1$$$, and thus the area is $$$3$$$. The other two have the answer $$$3$$$ to the query $$$x=1$$$.

 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c5dc08fb42418ce319b2c3014625eb141430162e.png) 

For the second sample case, there is only one candidate polygon, and thus the area is $$$1999/2$$$.



Note that the order of the vertices shown in the sample case may not be consistent with the actual provided.



The blank lines in the sample case are added for readability. In your output, extra spaces or blank lines will be ignored.

# # 猜多边形

这是一道交互题。



给定一个简单多边形，但在告诉你多边形的 $$$n$$$ 个顶点之前，小 Q 将它们打乱了。



现在你可以向小 Q 提出不超过 $$$(n-2)$$$ 次询问，每次询问由两个整数 $$$p$$$ 和 $$$q$$$ 组成（$$$0 \le p/q \le 1\,000, 1 \le q \le 1\,000$$$）。他会告诉你直线 $$$x=p/q$$$ 上位于多边形内部或边界上的点的总长度，该长度可以表示为 $$$r/s$$$，其中 $$$r$$$ 和 $$$s$$$ 为两个整数（$$$r \ge 0, s \ge 1, \gcd(r,s) = 1$$$）。这里 $$$\gcd(r,s)$$$ 是 $$$r$$$ 和 $$$s$$$ 的最大公约数。



你需要求出多边形的面积，面积同样可以表示为 $$$u/v$$$，其中 $$$u$$$ 和 $$$v$$$ 为两个整数（$$$u \ge 0, v \ge 1, \gcd(u,v) = 1$$$）。



多边形及其顶点的顺序在交互开始前就已确定，且不依赖于你的询问。换句话说，交互器不是自适应的。



## 输入



输入的第一行包含一个整数 $$$T$$$（$$$1 \le T \le 1\,000$$$），表示测试用例的数量。对于每个测试用例：



第一行包含一个整数 $$$n$$$（$$$3 \le n \le 1\,000$$$），表示多边形的顶点数。



接下来有 $$$n$$$ 行，每行包含两个整数 $$$x$$$ 和 $$$y$$$（$$$0 \le x,y \le 1\,000$$$），给出多边形顶点的坐标 $$$(x, y)$$$，顺序已打乱。



多边形是简单的，即其顶点互不相同，且多边形的任意两条边不相交也不接触，除非相邻的边在其公共顶点处接触。此外，任意两条相邻的边不共线。



保证所有测试用例中 $$$n$$$ 的总和不超过 $$$1\,000$$$。



## 交互



如果你想提出询问，输出一行。首先输出 `?` 后跟一个空格，然后输出两个整数 $$$p$$$ 和 $$$q$$$（$$$0 \le p/q \le 1\,000, 1 \le q \le 1\,000$$$）。刷新输出后，你的程序应读取两个整数 $$$r$$$ 和 $$$s$$$（$$$r \ge 0, s \ge 1, \gcd(r,s) = 1$$$），表示对你询问的答案。



如果你想猜多边形的面积，输出一行。首先输出 `!` 后跟一个空格，然后输出两个整数 $$$u$$$ 和 $$$v$$$（$$$u \ge 0, v \ge 1, \gcd(u,v) = 1$$$），表示多边形的面积为 $$$u/v$$$。刷新输出后，你的程序应继续处理下一个测试用例，如果没有更多测试用例则立即退出。注意你的猜测不计入询问次数。



要刷新输出，你可以使用：



- `fflush(stdout)`（如果在 C 和 C++ 中使用 `printf`）或 `cout.flush()`（如果在 C 和 C++ 中使用 `cout`）。

- `System.out.flush()` 在 Java 和 Kotlin 中。

- `sys.stdout.flush()` 在 Python 中。



## 注意



对于第一个样例，有三个候选多边形，如下图所示。只有最左边的一个满足查询 $$$x=1$$$ 的答案 $$$2$$$，因此面积为 $$$3$$$。另外两个对查询 $$$x=1$$$ 的答案为 $$$3$$$。

 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c5dc08fb42418ce319b2c3014625eb141430162e.png) 

对于第二个样例，只有一个候选多边形，因此面积为 $$$1999/2$$$。



注意，样例中显示的顶点顺序可能与实际提供的顺序不一致。



样例中的空行是为了提高可读性而添加的。在你的输出中，额外的空格或空行将被忽略。

# Make Them Believe

The 2024 League of Legends World Championship culminated in an epic clash between two titans of professional League of Legends on November 2, 2024. Bilibili Gaming, after dominating the LPL with two domestic titles in 2024, undoubtedly carried the hopes of China's premier league that had endured three years without lifting the Summoner's Cup. In their way stood T1, who had qualified as LCK's fourth seed but proved their championship mettle through their tournament run. And there he was — Faker, the man revered as "the highest mountain and the longest river" — still standing at the center of LoL's greatest stage as if time itself had learned to bow before him. With four crowns already weighing heavy in his legacy, Faker somehow made the hunt for a fifth feel less like ambition and more like destiny. Now, beneath the towering dome of London's O2 Arena, the stakes were immense for both teams: BLG aimed to end the LPL's drought and cement their remarkable 2024 campaign, while T1 sought to defend their title and further establish their dynasty.



In an electrifying best-of-five series that pushed both teams to their limits, T1 emerged victorious over BLG with a hard-fought 3-2 triumph, clinching their fifth world championship. True to the tournament's official slogan "Make Them Believe", T1 mounted an incredible comeback from a 1-2 deficit, reaffirming once again why they remain a seemingly insurmountable obstacle for LPL teams in the international arena.



As we trace back through the journey of these two finalist teams, it all started in that fateful knockout stage, where eight teams competed in a single-elimination tournament: LNG Esports, Weibo Gaming, Hanwha Life Esports, Bilibili Gaming, Top Esports, T1, Gen.G, and FlyQuest. In an eight-team single-elimination tournament format, teams were seeded into the bracket based on their performance in the Swiss stage to face off in head-to-head matches where the loser is immediately eliminated. The tournament progresses through three rounds: Quarterfinals with eight teams, Semifinals with four teams, and the Finals with two teams, ultimately crowning a single champion.

 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/fe32cee33eddd4c16680a56aa176b7c6131f7a08.png) Figure: Eight-Team Single-Elimination Tournament Bracket 

Although Worlds 2024 has irretrievably passed into history, we can still craft our own version of the story. For this problem, you will simulate a hypothetical knockout stage using the same eight-team single-elimination format. You will be given the names and the strength values of the eight teams in order from top to bottom of the Quarterfinals bracket (shown in the leftmost column in Figure), and both the names and the strength values are guaranteed to be pairwise different. When two teams compete, the team with the higher strength value always wins, while the losing team is eliminated. For two teams competing in the Finals, the team that wins is designated as the champion, while the other team is designated as the runner-up.



Your task is to find the champion team and the runner-up team in the hypothetical knockout stage.



## Input



The input contains eight lines, the $$$i$$$-th of which contains a string $$$S_i$$$ ($$$1 \leq |S_i| \leq 3$$$) and an integer $$$t_i$$$ ($$$1 \leq t_i \leq 100$$$), indicating the name and the strength value of the $$$i$$$-th team from top to bottom of the Quarterfinals bracket.



It is guaranteed that all team names contain only uppercase English letters or decimal digits, and both the names and the strength values are pairwise different.



## Output



Output "`A beats B`" (without quotes) in one line, where `A` is the name of the champion team and `B` is the name of the runner-up team.



## Note



In the second sample case, since we intentionally increase BLG's strength value in the hypothetical knockout stage, please note that the outcome of the Finals, sadly, differs from the actual Worlds 2024.

# 让他们相信

2024英雄联盟全球总决赛于2月2024日在一场史诗级的对决中落下帷幕，两支职业英雄联盟的巨擘展开了激烈碰撞。Bilibili Gaming在2024年统治LPL并斩获两个国内冠军后，无疑承载着中国顶级联赛的希望——该联赛已历经三年未能捧起召唤师杯。挡在他们面前的是T1，他们以LCK四号种子的身份晋级，却通过自己的赛事征程证明了冠军底蕴。而他就在那里——Faker，那位被尊为“最高的山，最长的河”的男人——依然屹立于英雄联盟最伟大舞台的中央，仿佛时间本身也学会了向他俯首。四座冠军奖杯早已沉甸甸地压在他的传奇之上，Faker却不知怎地让对第五冠的追逐显得不像雄心，而更像宿命。如今，在伦敦O2体育馆高耸的穹顶之下，对两支队伍而言赌注都无比巨大：BLG志在终结LPL的干旱期并巩固他们非凡的2024赛季，而T1则寻求卫冕并进一步奠定他们的王朝。



在一场激动人心的五局三胜系列赛中，双方都被逼到了极限，T1最终以一场艰苦卓绝的3-2胜利击败BLG，夺得队史第五座世界冠军。正如赛事官方口号“Make Them Believe”所言，T1从1-2的落后局面中上演了不可思议的逆转，再次印证了为何他们始终是LPL战队在国际赛场上看似难以逾越的障碍。



回顾这两支决赛队伍的征程，一切都要从那个决定命运的淘汰赛阶段说起，当时八支队伍参加了单败淘汰赛：LNG Esports、Weibo Gaming、Hanwha Life Esports、Bilibili Gaming、Top Esports、T1、Gen.G 和 FlyQuest。在八队单败淘汰赛制中，队伍根据瑞士轮阶段的表现被分入对阵表，进行正面对决，败者立即被淘汰。赛事共进行三轮：八队参加的 Quarterfinals、四队参加的 Semifinals，以及两队参加的 Finals，最终决出一支冠军队伍。

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/fe32cee33eddd4c16680a56aa176b7c6131f7a08.png) 图：八队单败淘汰赛对阵图

尽管 2024 年世界赛已成历史，我们仍可以编写自己的故事版本。对于本题，你将使用相同的八队单败淘汰赛制来模拟一个假设的淘汰赛阶段。你将得到四分之一决赛对阵表（如图中最左列所示）中从上到下八支队伍的名称和实力值，且名称和实力值均保证两两不同。当两支队伍比赛时，实力值更高的队伍总是获胜，而失败的队伍被淘汰。对于参加总决赛的两支队伍，获胜的队伍被指定为冠军，另一支队伍被指定为亚军。



你的任务是找出假想淘汰赛阶段中的冠军队伍和亚军队伍。



## 输入



输入包含八行，其中第$$$i$$$行包含一个字符串$$$S_i$$$（$$$1 \leq |S_i| \leq 3$$$）和一个整数$$$t_i$$$（$$$1 \leq t_i \leq 100$$$），表示四分之一决赛对阵表中从上到下第$$$i$$$支队伍的名称和实力值。



保证所有队伍名称仅包含大写英文字母或十进制数字，且所有名称和实力值均两两不同。



## 输出



在一行中输出“`A beats B`”（不含引号），其中`A`是冠军队伍的名称，`B`是亚军队伍的名称。



## 提示



在第二个样例中，由于我们在假设的淘汰赛阶段有意提高了BLG的实力值，请注意，遗憾的是，决赛结果与实际的世界赛2024不同。

# The Grand Contest

In the Grand Contest, there are many problems and a very long duration. Team $$$1$$$ and team $$$2$$$ participated in this contest, which had a total of $$$n$$$ submissions. Each submission can either get a correct or incorrect verdict. A problem is considered solved by a team when the submission from that team is correct.

After the contest ends, teams are ranked by the most problems solved. Teams that solve the same number of problems are ranked by the least total time. The total time is the sum of the time consumed for each solved problem. The time consumed for a solved problem is the time elapsed from the beginning of the contest to the submission of the first correct submission, plus $$$p$$$ penalty minutes for each previously incorrect submission for that problem. There is no time consumed for a problem that is not solved. In case of a tie, team $$$1$$$ ranks before team $$$2$$$.

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6a61531aed825433635e008b3a2d12940bde9d21.png)

The judges of the Grand Contest will test a feature named "remove interval", which allows selecting two integers $$$L$$$ and $$$R$$$ ($$$0 \le L \lt R$$$) and remove the time interval $$$[L,R]$$$ in minutes from the contest such that:

- All submissions with submission time less than $$$L$$$ minutes are unaffected;

- All submissions with submission time in $$$[L,R]$$$ minutes have their submission time changed to $$$L$$$ minutes from the beginning;

- All submissions with submission time more than $$$R$$$ minutes have their submission time reduced by $$$(R-L)$$$ minutes.

It is important to note that the above changes will only affect the submission times of certain submissions but will not affect the relative order of the submissions.

You need to find the shortest time interval $$$[L,R]$$$ in minutes such that after removing this interval from the contest, the rankings of the two teams will change, or indicate that such an interval does not exist. If there are multiple such intervals, you need to find the one with the smallest $$$L$$$.

## Input

The first line of the input contains an integer $$$T$$$ ($$$1 \le T \le 4 \times 10^5$$$), indicating the number of test cases. For each test case:

The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 4 \times 10^5$$$) and $$$p$$$ ($$$1 \le p \le 10^{12}$$$), indicating the number of submissions and the penalty minutes.

Then $$$n$$$ lines follow, describing the submissions during the contest in order. Each line contains four integers $$$a$$$ ($$$a \in \{1,2\}$$$), $$$b$$$ ($$$1 \le b \le 10^9$$$), $$$c$$$ ($$$1 \le c \le 10^{12}$$$), and $$$d$$$ ($$$d \in \{0,1\}$$$), indicating team $$$a$$$ submitted on problem $$$b$$$ at $$$c$$$ minutes from the beginning of the contest and got verdict $$$d$$$. If $$$d=1$$$, the submission is correct and solves the problem; otherwise, the submission is incorrect. It is guaranteed that the submission time is non-decreasing.

It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$4 \times 10^5$$$.

## Output

For each test case, output a line. If there exists a feasible time interval in minutes, output two integers $$$L$$$ and $$$R$$$, indicating the shortest interval with the smallest $$$L$$$. Otherwise, output $$$-1$$$.

# The Grand Contest

在 Grand Contest 中，有许多题目，并且比赛持续时间非常长。队伍 $$$1$$$ 和队伍 $$$2$$$ 参加了这场比赛，比赛总共有 $$$n$$$ 次提交。每次提交可能得到正确或错误的判定。当某支队伍的提交正确时，该队伍就被认为解决了该题。

比赛结束后，队伍按解题数量从多到少排名。解题数量相同的队伍按总用时从少到多排名。总用时是每道已解决题目所消耗时间之和。一道已解决题目所消耗的时间，是从比赛开始到该题第一次正确提交所经过的时间，再加上该题此前每次错误提交的 $$$p$$$ 罚时分钟。未解决的题目不计时间。如果仍然并列，队伍 $$$1$$$ 排在队伍 $$$2$$$ 之前。

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6a61531aed825433635e008b3a2d12940bde9d21.png)

Grand Contest 的裁判将测试一个名为“移除区间”的功能，它允许选择两个整数 $$$L$$$ 和 $$$R$$$（$$$0 \le L \lt R$$$），并从比赛中移除时间区间 $$$[L,R]$$$ 分钟，使得：

- 所有提交时间小于 $$$L$$$ 分钟的提交不受影响；

- 所有提交时间在 $$$[L,R]$$$ 分钟内的提交，其提交时间变为从比赛开始算起的 $$$L$$$ 分钟；

- 所有提交时间大于 $$$R$$$ 分钟的提交，其提交时间减少 $$$(R-L)$$$ 分钟。

需要注意的是，上述更改只会影响某些提交的提交时间，但不会影响提交之间的相对顺序。

你需要找到最短的时间区间 $$$[L,R]$$$ 分钟，使得从比赛中移除该区间后，两支队伍的排名会发生变化，或者指出这样的区间不存在。如果存在多个这样的区间，你需要找到 $$$L$$$ 最小的那个。

## 输入

输入的第一行包含一个整数 $$$T$$$（$$$1 \le T \le 4 \times 10^5$$$），表示测试用例的数量。对于每个测试用例：

第一行包含两个整数 $$$n$$$（$$$1 \le n \le 4 \times 10^5$$$）和 $$$p$$$（$$$1 \le p \le 10^{12}$$$），分别表示提交数量和罚时分钟数。

接下来有 $$$n$$$ 行，按顺序描述比赛期间的提交。每行包含四个整数 $$$a$$$（$$$a \in \{1,2\}$$$）、$$$b$$$（$$$1 \le b \le 10^9$$$）、$$$c$$$（$$$1 \le c \le 10^{12}$$$）和 $$$d$$$（$$$d \in \{0,1\}$$$），表示队伍 $$$a$$$ 在比赛开始后第 $$$c$$$ 分钟于题目 $$$b$$$ 上提交，并得到评测结果 $$$d$$$。如果 $$$d=1$$$，则该提交正确并解决了该题；否则，该提交不正确。保证提交时间非递减。

保证所有测试用例中 $$$n$$$ 的总和不超过 $$$4 \times 10^5$$$。

## 输出

对于每个测试用例，输出一行。如果存在可行的分钟时间区间，输出两个整数 $$$L$$$ 和 $$$R$$$，表示具有最小 $$$L$$$ 的最短区间。否则，输出 $$$-1$$$。

# Obliviate, Then Reincarnate

Leafing through his journal of musings, Mu discovered a note forgotten between the yellowed pages. The note, inspired by the faraway constellation Vulpecula, resembled a mantra of self-encouragement which read, "Dreams are like the stars, distant and sometimes insignificant, yet enough to spark up the darkest night."



In time, Mu had eventually glimpsed the veiled face of dreams. Through years of growth, he had emerged more seasoned, perhaps more scarred, only to accept that stars and dreams alike, constrained by the fatalism that equally governs everything, are destined to fade into oblivion. Pursuit of dreams had crumbled, doubt about reality had shadowed, yet in his refusal to succumb to pessimism, Mu had waited, and was waiting still, harboring the belief that broken dreams, like stellar ashes in the pageantry of samsara, would be reconstructed and kindled anew.



He continued reviewing the journal, with the boundless cosmos reigning overhead. Indeed, the infinite had always held more promise and mystery than the finite — be it in the realm of spacetime, in the nebula of dreams, or even in the world of mathematics. As if on cue, his fingers paused at a page where Hilbert's Hotel Paradox, the classic paradigm of infinite sets, had once captured his contemplation. Amid the jottings, Mu had envisioned an upgraded version of the infinite hotel — the Celestial Hilbert's Hotel — and cast himself as its manager, leaving an intriguing problem for programmers like you to solve.

 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/fc33a6de12a20dc559daeac03b4bb18aaaebb034.png) Hilbert's Infinite Hotel 

As a marvel of deep space, the Celestial Hilbert's Hotel features infinitely many rooms. Each room is assigned a unique integer (can be positive, negative, or zero) as its number, and all the room numbers constitute $$$\mathbb{Z}$$$, the set of all integers.



There are $$$n$$$ floors in the hotel, where rooms are distributed based on the non-negative remainder of their number when divided by $$$n$$$. Specifically, room $$$x$$$ and room $$$y$$$ are on the same floor if and only if the room numbers have the common remainder when divided by $$$n$$$, expressed as a congruence equation $$$x \equiv y \pmod n$$$.



Like any typical Hilbert's Hotel, the version in question also operates with certain relocation instructions to vacate occupied rooms. Mu has designed $$$m$$$ relocation instructions. Each instruction, denoted as a pair $$$(a, b)$$$, directs all guests on the same floor as room $$$a$$$ to simultaneously move to new rooms by adding $$$b$$$ to their previous room numbers. When necessary, Mu can select one of these $$$m$$$ instructions and broadcast it to the corresponding floor. You might wonder about the case where guests are asked to move into already occupied rooms. In this scenario, the relocating guests will still move in, accompanying the original occupants forever.



However, due to the infinity of the Celestial Hilbert's Hotel, it is hard for Mu to track a guest's potential locations after multiple instructions, resulting in management inefficiency. Thus, Mu proposes $$$q$$$ queries, each concerning a guest who initially occupies room $$$x$$$. Supposing that the relocation instructions can be applied any number of times in any order, with both the exact number of times and order being unspecified, for each query, your task is to determine whether the set of all room numbers possibly reachable by the guest concerned is an infinite set. More formally, let $$$S_k$$$ be the set of room numbers possibly reachable by the guest concerned after at most $$$k$$$ instructions, then you need to determine whether for all integers $$$t$$$, such $$$k$$$ exists that $$$|S_k| \gt t$$$ can be achieved, where $$$|S_k|$$$ denotes the size of $$$S_k$$$.



## Input



The first line contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, and $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le n, m, q \le 5 \times 10^5$$$), indicating the number of floors, relocation instructions, and queries, respectively.



Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each of which contains two integers $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ ($$$-10^9 \le a, b \le 10^9$$$), describing a relocation instruction $$$(a, b)$$$.



Then $$$q$$$ lines follow, each of which contains an integer $$$x$$$ ($$$-10^9 \le x \le 10^9$$$), indicating a query concerning the guest who initially occupies room $$$x$$$.



## Output



For each query, output "`Yes`" (without quotes) in one line if the set of all room numbers possibly reachable by the guest concerned is an infinite set, or otherwise output "`No`" (without quotes) in one line.

# 遗忘，然后转生

翻阅着自己的思绪日记，Mu 发现了一张被遗忘在泛黄书页间的纸条。这张受遥远星座狐狸座启发的纸条，像是一句自我鼓励的箴言，上面写着：“梦想就像星辰，遥远而有时微不足道，却足以点燃最黑暗的夜晚。”



随着时间的推移，Mu 终于瞥见了梦想那蒙着面纱的脸。经过多年的成长，他变得更加老练，也许更加伤痕累累，却只能接受星辰与梦想一样，都受制于同样支配万物的宿命论，注定要消逝于遗忘之中。对梦想的追求已经崩塌，对现实的怀疑已经笼罩，然而在拒绝向悲观屈服的过程中，Mu 曾经等待过，现在仍在等待，怀抱着一种信念：破碎的梦想，如同轮回盛景中的星辰灰烬，将会被重建并重新点燃。



他继续翻阅日记，无垠的宇宙高悬于头顶。的确，无限总是比有限承载着更多的希望与神秘——无论是在时空的领域中，在梦想的星云里，还是在数学的世界里。仿佛应和着某种召唤，他的手指停在了一页上，那里曾有一度吸引他沉思的希尔伯特旅馆悖论——无限集合的经典范式。在那些笔记之间，Mu 构想了一个升级版的无限旅馆——天界希尔伯特旅馆——并把自己设想为它的经理，留下了一个有趣的问题，让像你这样的程序员来解决。

 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/fc33a6de12a20dc559daeac03b4bb18aaaebb034.png) 希尔伯特无限旅馆 

作为深空的奇迹，天界希尔伯特旅馆拥有无限多个房间。每个房间都被分配一个唯一的整数（可以是正数、负数或零）作为其编号，而所有房间编号构成了 $$$\mathbb{Z}$$$，即所有整数的集合。



旅馆有 $$$n$$$ 层，房间根据其编号除以 $$$n$$$ 时的非负余数进行分布。具体来说，房间 $$$x$$$ 和房间 $$$y$$$ 在同一层，当且仅当这两个房间编号除以 $$$n$$$ 时具有相同的余数，表示为同余方程 $$$x \equiv y \pmod n$$$。



像任何典型的希尔伯特旅馆一样，这里的版本也通过某些搬迁指令来腾出已占用的房间。Mu 设计了 $$$m$$$ 条搬迁指令。每条指令表示为一对 $$$(a, b)$$$，指示与房间 $$$a$$$ 在同一层的所有客人同时搬迁到新房间，方法是在他们之前的房间编号上加上 $$$b$$$。必要时，Mu 可以选择这些 $$$m$$$ 条指令中的一条，并向相应楼层广播。你可能会想，如果客人被要求搬入已经有人入住的房间会怎样。在这种情况下，搬迁的客人仍然会搬进去，并永远陪伴原来的住户。



然而，由于天界希尔伯特旅馆的无限性，Mu 很难在多次指令之后追踪一位客人可能的位置，从而导致管理效率低下。因此，Mu 提出了 $$$q$$$ 个询问，每个询问都关于一位初始时住在房间 $$$x$$$ 的客人。假设这些搬迁指令可以以任意顺序应用任意多次，且具体次数和顺序均未指定，对于每个询问，你的任务是判断该客人所有可能到达的房间编号构成的集合是否为无限集。更形式化地，令 $$$S_k$$$ 表示该客人至多经过 $$$k$$$ 条指令后所有可能到达的房间编号构成的集合，那么你需要判断是否对于所有整数 $$$t$$$，都存在这样的 $$$k$$$，使得 $$$|S_k| \gt t$$$ 能够成立，其中 $$$|S_k|$$$ 表示 $$$S_k$$$ 的大小。



## 输入



第一行包含三个整数 $$$n$$$、$$$m$$$ 和 $$$q$$$（$$$1 \le n, m, q \le 5 \times 10^5$$$），分别表示楼层数、搬迁指令数和询问数。



接下来有 $$$m$$$ 行，每行包含两个整数 $$$a$$$ 和 $$$b$$$（$$$-10^9 \le a, b \le 10^9$$$），描述一条搬迁指令 $$$(a, b)$$$。



接下来有 $$$q$$$ 行，每行包含一个整数 $$$x$$$（$$$-10^9 \le x \le 10^9$$$），表示一个关于初始时住在房间 $$$x$$$ 的客人的询问。



## 输出



对于每个询问，如果该客人所有可能到达的房间编号构成的集合是无限集，则在一行中输出 "`Yes`"（不含引号），否则在一行中输出 "`No`"（不含引号）。

# Antivirus

In the introduction to network flow, the teacher had barely begun explaining when their pet chicken figured out how to solve the problem. The teacher exclaimed: Our avian flu is amazing!

—Roasted-chicken

Hyrule is entering the flu season.

Hyrule consists of $$$n$$$ cities, which are connected by $$$m$$$ directed roads. The capital (city numbered $$$1$$$) can be reached from all cities through these roads.

The flu season will last for $$$q$$$ days. On the $$$i$$$-th day at noon, the flu virus will start spreading from city $$$a_i$$$. The virus will spread along the roads to other cities. The virus spreads very quickly, so it can be assumed that all cities reachable from $$$a_i$$$ will be infected immediately. As the capital city of Hyrule, city $$$1$$$ is crucial for the whole country. If the virus that starts spreading on the $$$i$$$-th day reaches the capital, there will be an economic loss cost of $$$b_i$$$.

To prevent the virus from spreading, Auru can deploy a virus filter in a city each night (including the night before the first day). Deploying a virus filter in city $$$i$$$ has a deployment cost of $$$c_i$$$. The virus cannot spread through the city equipped with a virus filter, and that city will also remain uninfected. If the virus were to start spreading from a city equipped with a virus filter, the virus would simply disappear without infecting any cities. The deployed virus filter remains effective until Auru deploys a new filter in another city. (In other words, there can be at most one virus filter at a time.)

Auru wants to know: for each $$$i = 1, 2, \dots, q$$$, considering only the viruses in the first $$$i$$$ days, what is the minimum value of "economic loss cost + deployment cost".

## Input

Each test file contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$T$$$ ($$$1 \leq T \leq 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, and $$$q$$$ ($$$2 \leq n \leq 10^5$$$, $$$n-1 \leq m \leq 2 \times 10^5$$$, $$$1 \leq q \leq 10^5$$$), representing the number of cities, the number of roads, and the duration of the flu season in days, respectively.

In the next $$$m$$$ lines, each contains two integers $$$u_i$$$ and $$$v_i$$$ ($$$1 \leq u_i, v_i \leq n$$$), representing a directed road from city $$$u_i$$$ to city $$$v_i$$$. It is guaranteed that there are no self-loops, but there may be multiple edges between cities. The capital can be reached from all cities.

The next line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$c_1, c_2, \dots, c_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq c_i \leq 10^9$$$), representing the deployment cost of the virus filter in each city.

In the following $$$q$$$ lines, the $$$i$$$-th one contains two integers $$$a_i$$$ and $$$b_i$$$ ($$$2 \leq a_i \leq n$$$, $$$1 \leq b_i \leq 10^9$$$), indicating the city where the virus starts to spread on the $$$i$$$-th day and the economic loss cost if the virus reaches the capital.

For each test file, it is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^5$$$, the sum of $$$m$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \times 10^5$$$, and the sum of $$$q$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^5$$$.

## Output

For each test case, output a line containing $$$n$$$ integers, where the $$$i$$$-th integer represents the minimum value of the "economic loss cost + deployment cost" when only considering the viruses in the first $$$i$$$ days.

## Note

In the first test case:

- The minimum cost after day $$$1$$$ is $$$2$$$: on night $$$0$$$, deploy a virus filter in city $$$4$$$ with a deployment cost of $$$2$$$.

- The minimum cost after day $$$2$$$ is $$$3$$$: on night $$$0$$$, deploy a virus filter in city $$$2$$$ with a deployment cost of $$$3$$$.

- The minimum cost after day $$$3$$$ is $$$4$$$: on night $$$0$$$, deploy a virus filter in city $$$2$$$ with a deployment cost of $$$3$$$; on night $$$2$$$, deploy a virus filter in city $$$6$$$ with a deployment cost of $$$1$$$.

- The minimum cost after day $$$4$$$ is $$$4$$$: on night $$$0$$$, deploy a virus filter in city $$$1$$$ with a deployment cost of $$$4$$$.

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b07226638d09c43213254287f7c4ecf8d517edb2.png)

Example $$$1$$$ Illustration

In the second test case:

- The minimum cost after day $$$1$$$ is $$$5$$$: on night $$$0$$$, deploy a virus filter in city $$$5$$$ with a deployment cost of $$$5$$$.

- The minimum cost after day $$$2$$$ is $$$100$$$: on night $$$0$$$, deploy a virus filter in city $$$4$$$ with a deployment cost of $$$100$$$.

- The minimum cost after day $$$3$$$ is $$$102$$$: on night $$$0$$$, deploy a virus filter in city $$$4$$$ with a deployment cost of $$$100$$$; on night $$$2$$$, deploy a virus filter in city $$$3$$$ with a deployment cost of $$$2$$$.

- The minimum cost after day $$$4$$$ is $$$202$$$: on night $$$0$$$, deploy a virus filter in city $$$4$$$ with a deployment cost of $$$100$$$; on night $$$2$$$, deploy a virus filter in city $$$3$$$ with a deployment cost of $$$2$$$; on night $$$3$$$, deploy a virus filter in city $$$4$$$ again with a deployment cost of $$$100$$$.

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d1443a272588d452e06ae517d6da03e9596de3a6.png)

Example $$$2$$$ Illustration

In the third test case, since only one virus filter can exist at a time, it is not possible to stop the virus from spreading by deploying virus filters in both cities $$$2$$$ and $$$3$$$. The deployment costs for cities $$$1$$$ and $$$4$$$ are higher than the economic loss cost caused by the virus, so no virus filter is deployed, and the minimum cost is $$$10$$$ (economic loss cost).

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/74ff34b8b543c0c94f5fabf4a0065bd5c527d495.png)

Example $$$3$$$ Illustration

在网络流的入门课上，老师刚讲到一半，他们养的鸡就已经会做这道题了。老师惊呼：我们的禽流感太厉害了！

——烤鸡

海拉鲁进入了流感季。

海拉鲁由$$$n$$$座城市组成，这些城市之间由$$$m$$$条有向道路连接。从所有城市都可以通过这些道路到达首都（编号为$$$1$$$的城市）。

流感季将持续$$$q$$$天。在第$$$i$$$天中午，流感病毒将从城市$$$a_i$$$开始传播。病毒会沿着道路传播到其他城市。病毒传播得非常快，因此可以认为从$$$a_i$$$可达的所有城市都会立即被感染。作为海拉鲁的首都，城市$$$1$$$对整个国家至关重要。如果第$$$i$$$天开始传播的病毒到达了首都，就会造成$$$b_i$$$的经济损失。

为了防止病毒传播，Auru每天晚上（包括第一天之前的晚上）可以在一个城市部署病毒过滤器。在城市$$$i$$$部署病毒过滤器的部署费用为$$$c_i$$$。病毒无法通过部署了病毒过滤器的城市传播，该城市也将保持不被感染。如果病毒从部署了病毒过滤器的城市开始传播，病毒会直接消失，不会感染任何城市。已部署的病毒过滤器会一直有效，直到Auru在另一个城市部署新的过滤器。（换句话说，同一时间最多只能有一个病毒过滤器。）

Auru想知道：对于每个$$$i = 1, 2, \dots, q$$$，只考虑前$$$i$$$天内的病毒，“经济损失 + 部署费用”的最小值是多少。

## 输入

每个测试文件包含多个测试用例。第一行包含测试用例数$$$T$$$（$$$1 \leq T \leq 10^4$$$）。接下来是测试用例的描述。

第一行包含三个整数$$$n$$$、$$$m$$$和$$$q$$$（$$$2 \leq n \leq 10^5$$$，$$$n-1 \leq m \leq 2 \times 10^5$$$，$$$1 \leq q \leq 10^5$$$），分别表示城市数、道路数和流感季持续天数。

接下来$$$m$$$行，每行包含两个整数$$$u_i$$$和$$$v_i$$$（$$$1 \leq u_i, v_i \leq n$$$），表示一条从城市$$$u_i$$$到城市$$$v_i$$$的有向道路。保证没有自环，但城市之间可能存在多条边。从所有城市都可以到达首都。

下一行包含$$$n$$$个整数$$$c_1, c_2, \dots, c_n$$$（$$$1 \leq c_i \leq 10^9$$$），表示每个城市部署病毒过滤器的费用。

在接下来的 $$$q$$$ 行中，第 $$$i$$$ 行包含两个整数 $$$a_i$$$ 和 $$$b_i$$$（$$$2 \leq a_i \leq n$$$，$$$1 \leq b_i \leq 10^9$$$），表示病毒在第 $$$i$$$ 天开始传播的城市，以及如果病毒到达首都时的经济损失费用。

对于每个测试文件，保证所有测试用例中 $$$n$$$ 的总和不超过 $$$10^5$$$，所有测试用例中 $$$m$$$ 的总和不超过 $$$2 \times 10^5$$$，且所有测试用例中 $$$q$$$ 的总和不超过 $$$10^5$$$。

## 输出

对于每个测试用例，输出一行包含 $$$n$$$ 个整数，其中第 $$$i$$$ 个整数表示仅考虑前 $$$i$$$ 天中的病毒时，“经济损失费用 + 部署费用”的最小值。

## 说明

在第一个测试用例中：

- 第 $$$1$$$ 天后的最小费用为 $$$2$$$：在第 $$$0$$$ 天晚上，在城市 $$$4$$$ 部署一个病毒过滤器，部署费用为 $$$2$$$。

- 第 $$$2$$$ 天后的最小费用为 $$$3$$$：在第 $$$0$$$ 天晚上，在城市 $$$2$$$ 部署一个病毒过滤器，部署费用为 $$$3$$$。

- 第 $$$3$$$ 天后的最小费用为 $$$4$$$：在第 $$$0$$$ 天晚上，在城市 $$$2$$$ 部署一个病毒过滤器，部署费用为 $$$3$$$；在第 $$$2$$$ 天晚上，在城市 $$$6$$$ 部署一个病毒过滤器，部署费用为 $$$1$$$。

- 第 $$$4$$$ 天后的最小费用为 $$$4$$$：在第 $$$0$$$ 天晚上，在城市 $$$1$$$ 部署一个病毒过滤器，部署费用为 $$$4$$$。

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b07226638d09c43213254287f7c4ecf8d517edb2.png)

示例 $$$1$$$ 说明

在第二个测试用例中：

- 第 $$$1$$$ 天后的最小费用为 $$$5$$$：在第 $$$0$$$ 天晚上，在城市 $$$5$$$ 部署一个病毒过滤器，部署费用为 $$$5$$$。

- 第 $$$2$$$ 天后的最小费用为 $$$100$$$：在第 $$$0$$$ 天晚上，在城市 $$$4$$$ 部署一个病毒过滤器，部署费用为 $$$100$$$。

- 第 $$$3$$$ 天后的最小费用为 $$$102$$$：在第 $$$0$$$ 天晚上，在城市 $$$4$$$ 部署一个病毒过滤器，部署成本为 $$$100$$$；在第 $$$2$$$ 天晚上，在城市 $$$3$$$ 部署一个病毒过滤器，部署成本为 $$$2$$$。

- 第 $$$4$$$ 天之后的最小成本为 $$$202$$$：在第 $$$0$$$ 天晚上，在城市 $$$4$$$ 部署一个病毒过滤器，部署成本为 $$$100$$$；在第 $$$2$$$ 天晚上，在城市 $$$3$$$ 部署一个病毒过滤器，部署成本为 $$$2$$$；在第 $$$3$$$ 天晚上，再次在城市 $$$4$$$ 部署一个病毒过滤器，部署成本为 $$$100$$$。

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d1443a272588d452e06ae517d6da03e9596de3a6.png)

示例 $$$2$$$ 说明

在第三个测试用例中，由于同一时间只能存在一个病毒过滤器，因此不可能通过在城市 $$$2$$$ 和 $$$3$$$ 中都部署病毒过滤器来阻止病毒传播。城市 $$$1$$$ 和 $$$4$$$ 的部署成本高于病毒造成的经济损失成本，因此不部署病毒过滤器，最小成本为 $$$10$$$（经济损失成本）。

# Brackets

Originally, there were only three kinds of brackets. But due to the harsh realities of life, the greater-than and less-than signs started moonlighting as angle brackets.

—Stir-fried-chicken

Betty has a bracket sequence $$$s$$$ of length $$$n$$$, which consists of eight types of brackets: "`()[]{}<>`". Additionally, she has $$$m$$$ sub-bracket sequences, and the $$$i$$$-th sub-bracket sequence $$$t_i$$$ is the sequence formed by concatenating the characters from the $$$l_i$$$-th to the $$$r_i$$$-th position of $$$s$$$, i.e., $$$t_i = s_{l_i}s_{l_i+1} \cdots s_{r_i}$$$.

Betty wants to know, by taking out several pairs from these $$$m$$$ sub-bracket sequences and concatenating sequences in the same pair, how many valid bracket sequences$$$^\dagger$$$ can be formed at most? Formally, you need to find as many pairs $$$(a_i, b_i)$$$ as possible such that:

- For any integer $$$x$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$m$$$, the sum of its occurrences in $$$a$$$ and its occurrences in $$$b$$$ should be no larger than $$$1$$$.

- For any pair $$$(a_i, b_i)$$$, $$$t_{a_i}t_{b_i}$$$ is a valid bracket sequence$$$^\dagger$$$.

$$$^\dagger$$$ A bracket sequence $$$x$$$ is valid if and only if it satisfies one of the following conditions:

- $$$|x| = 0$$$, i.e., $$$x$$$ is an empty string.

- $$$x = LyR$$$, where $$$y$$$ is a valid bracket sequence, and $$$L$$$, $$$R$$$ are left and right brackets of the same type (i.e., $$$L=$$$ "`(`" and $$$R=$$$ "`)`", or $$$L=$$$ "`[`" and $$$R=$$$ "`]`", or $$$L=$$$ "`{`" and $$$R=$$$ "`}`", or $$$L=$$$ "`<`" and $$$R=$$$ "`>`").

- $$$x = y_1y_2$$$, where both $$$y_1$$$ and $$$y_2$$$ are valid bracket sequences.

## Input

Each test file contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$T$$$ ($$$1 \leq T \leq 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \leq n, m \leq 5 \times 10^5$$$), which represent the length of $$$s$$$ and the number of sub-bracket sequences, respectively.

The second line contains a string $$$s$$$ ($$$|s| = n$$$), which consists only of the eight brackets "`()[]{}<>`".

The next $$$m$$$ lines each contain two integers $$$l_i$$$ and $$$r_i$$$ ($$$1 \leq l_i \leq r_i \leq n$$$).

For each test file, it is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$5 \times 10^5$$$, and the sum of $$$m$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$5 \times 10^5$$$.

## Output

For each test case, output a single integer on a new line, representing the maximum number of valid bracket sequences that can be obtained by concatenating pairs of sub-bracket sequences.

## Note

In the first test case, $$$t_1=$$$ "`[]{}`". Although $$$t_1$$$ is already a valid bracket sequence, there are no other sub-bracket sequences that can be paired with it, so the output is $$$0$$$.

In the second test case, there are six sub-bracket sequences containing three "`(`" and three "`)`", which can be used to form three valid bracket sequences "`()`". Therefore, the output should be $$$3$$$.

In the third test case, no valid bracket sequences can be formed.

In the fourth test case, one possible matching is $$$t_1t_2$$$: "`{}««`" + "`»»`", and $$$t_4t_5$$$: "`{}`" + "`{()}`".

# Brackets

最初只有三种括号。但由于生活的严酷现实，大于号和小于号开始兼职当尖括号。

——爆炒鸡肉

Betty 有一个长度为 $$$n$$$ 的括号序列 $$$s$$$，它由八种括号组成："`()[]{}<>`"。此外，她有 $$$m$$$ 个子括号序列，第 $$$i$$$ 个子括号序列 $$$t_i$$$ 是由 $$$s$$$ 的第 $$$l_i$$$ 个到第 $$$r_i$$$ 个位置的字符拼接而成的序列，即 $$$t_i = s_{l_i}s_{l_i+1} \cdots s_{r_i}$$$。

Betty 想知道，从这 $$$m$$$ 个子括号序列中取出若干对，并将同一对中的序列拼接起来，最多能形成多少个合法的括号序列$$$^\dagger$$$？形式化地，你需要找到尽可能多的对 $$$(a_i, b_i)$$$，使得：

- 对于从 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$m$$$ 的任意整数 $$$x$$$，它在 $$$a$$$ 中的出现次数与在 $$$b$$$ 中的出现次数之和不超过 $$$1$$$。

- 对于任意一对 $$$(a_i, b_i)$$$，$$$t_{a_i}t_{b_i}$$$ 是一个合法的括号序列$$$^\dagger$$$。

$$$^\dagger$$$ 一个括号序列 $$$x$$$ 是合法的当且仅当它满足以下条件之一：

- $$$|x| = 0$$$，即 $$$x$$$ 是空串。

- $$$x = LyR$$$，其中 $$$y$$$ 是合法的括号序列，且 $$$L$$$、$$$R$$$ 是同一类型的左右括号（即 $$$L=$$$ "`(`" 和 $$$R=$$$ "`)`"，或 $$$L=$$$ "`[`" 和 $$$R=$$$ "`]`"，或 $$$L=$$$ "`{`" 和 $$$R=$$$ "`}`"，或 $$$L=$$$ "`<`" 和 $$$R=$$$ "`>`"）。

- $$$x = y_1y_2$$$，其中 $$$y_1$$$ 和 $$$y_2$$$ 都是合法的括号序列。

## 输入

每个测试文件包含多个测试用例。第一行包含测试用例数 $$$T$$$（$$$1 \leq T \leq 10^4$$$）。测试用例的描述如下。

第一行包含两个整数 $$$n$$$ 和 $$$m$$$（$$$1 \leq n, m \leq 5 \times 10^5$$$），分别表示 $$$s$$$ 的长度和子括号序列的数量。

第二行包含一个字符串 $$$s$$$（$$$|s| = n$$$），仅由八个括号 "`()[]{}<>`" 组成。

接下来的 $$$m$$$ 行每行包含两个整数 $$$l_i$$$ 和 $$$r_i$$$（$$$1 \leq l_i \leq r_i \leq n$$$）。

对于每个测试文件，保证所有测试用例中 $$$n$$$ 的总和不超过 $$$5 \times 10^5$$$，且所有测试用例中 $$$m$$$ 的总和不超过 $$$5 \times 10^5$$$。

## 输出

对于每个测试用例，在新的一行输出一个整数，表示通过拼接子括号序列对所能得到的合法括号序列的最大数量。

## 提示

在第一个测试用例中，$$$t_1=$$$ "`[]{}`"。虽然 $$$t_1$$$ 本身已经是合法括号序列，但没有其他子括号序列可以与它配对，因此输出为 $$$0$$$。

在第二个测试用例中，有六个包含三个 "`(`" 和三个 "`)`" 的子括号序列，可以组成三个合法括号序列 "`()`"。因此，输出应为 $$$3$$$。

在第三个测试用例中，无法组成任何合法括号序列。

在第四个测试用例中，一种可能的匹配是 $$$t_1t_2$$$："`{}««`" + "`»»`"，以及 $$$t_4t_5$$$："`{}`" + "`{()}`"。

# Coin

The government decided to cut the navy's budget and distribute the saved gold directly to the pirates. This managed to eliminate more pirates than the navy ever did.



—Boiled-chicken



The pirates have just seized a giant gold coin!



To determine the ownership of this gold coin, they decided to select the owner using the following method:



Let the current number of remaining pirates be $$$n$$$. The pirates line up in a queue, and the pirates at positions $$$1, 1+k, 1+2k, \dots, 1+(\lceil\frac{n}{k}\rceil - 1) k$$$ are eliminated. This operation is repeated until only one pirate remains. The final remaining pirate will receive the gold coin.



Charlie is the smartest among the pirates. He wants to know where he should stand initially to be the last pirate remaining and win the coin.



## Input



Each test file contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$T$$$ ($$$1 \leq T \leq 100$$$). The description of the test cases follows.



The first line of each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$2 \leq n, k \leq 10^{12}$$$), representing the initial number of pirates and the parameter used for elimination.



For each test file, it is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^{12}$$$, and the sum of $$$k$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^{12}$$$.



## Output



For each test case, output a single integer on a new line, indicating the position of the pirate who will ultimately receive the gold coin in the initial queue.



## Note



For the first test case in the example, the positions of the remaining pirates in the original sequence after each round are:



- Initial state: $$$1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6$$$.

- After the first round: $$$2, 4, 6$$$.

- After the second round: $$$4$$$.



For the second test case in the example, the positions of the remaining pirates in the original sequence after each round are:

- After the first round: $$$2, 3, 5, 6, 8$$$.

- After the second round: $$$3, 5, 8$$$.

- After the third round: $$$5, 8$$$.

# 金币

政府决定削减海军预算，把省下来的金币直接分给海盗。这消灭的海盗比海军以往消灭的还多。

海盗们刚刚抢到了一枚巨大的金币！



为了确定这枚金币的归属，他们决定用以下方法选出所有者：



设当前剩余海盗人数为$$$n$$$。海盗们排成一队，位置为$$$1, 1+k, 1+2k, \dots, 1+(\lceil\frac{n}{k}\rceil - 1) k$$$的海盗被淘汰。重复此操作，直到只剩一名海盗。最后剩下的海盗将获得金币。

## 输入

# Extracting Weights

"Emily is very busy"... I feel like Emily is actually pretty free.



—Grilled-chicken



This is an interactive problem.



Emily has a tree containing $$$n$$$ nodes, where the weight of the node numbered $$$i$$$ is $$$w_i$$$. Node $$$1$$$ is the root node, and the weight of the root node is $$$0$$$.



Emily wants you to guess the weight of each node. Specifically, you can make at most $$$n$$$ queries, with the $$$i$$$-th query containing two integers $$$u_i$$$ and $$$v_i$$$. If the simple path from $$$u_i$$$ to $$$v_i$$$ contains exactly $$$k$$$ edges, Emily will tell you the bitwise XOR$$$^{\dagger}$$$ of the weights of all the nodes on the simple path from node $$$u_i$$$ to node $$$v_i$$$ (including the endpoints). Otherwise, Emily will respond with "-1", indicating that she does not want to answer that question. Emily is very busy, so she will not start answering until you have asked all your questions.



Of course, you may not be able to guess the weights of all nodes with no more than $$$n$$$ queries for some cases. In such cases, you should not make any queries and instead directly tell Emily that it is impossible.



$$$^{\dagger}$$$The bitwise XOR operation refers to the addition of each bit of two binary numbers under modulo $$$2$$$. For example: $$$(0011)_2$$$ $$$\oplus$$$ $$$(0101)_2$$$ $$$=$$$ $$$(0110)_2$$$.



## Input



There is only one test case in each test file.



The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$2 \leq n \leq 250$$$, $$$1 \leq k \leq n-1$$$), representing the number of nodes in the tree and a parameter mentioned in the query.



The next $$$n-1$$$ lines each contain two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \leq x_i, y_i \leq n$$$), indicating that there is an edge between nodes $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$.



It is guaranteed that all edges form a tree, and the correct answer satisfies $$$0 \leq w_i \lt 2^{30}$$$.



## Interaction



First, you need to determine whether it is possible to guess the weights of all nodes within $$$n$$$ queries. If not, your program should output "`No`" and exit immediately. Otherwise, your program should output "`Yes`" and proceed to querying. You can output the answer in any case (upper or lower). For example, the strings "`yEs`", "`yes`", "`Yes`", and "`YES`" will be recognized as positive responses.



To make a query, output all your $$$q$$$ queries at once in the format "`? $$$q$$$ $$$u_1$$$ $$$v_1$$$ $$$u_2$$$ $$$v_2$$$ $$$\dots$$$ $$$u_q$$$ $$$v_q$$$`" ($$$1 \leq q \leq n$$$, $$$1 \leq u_i, v_i \leq n$$$). After flushing your output, your program should read a line containing $$$q$$$ integers. The $$$i$$$-th integer represents the response to the $$$i$$$-th query.



To guess the weights, output your guess in the format "`! $$$w_2$$$ $$$w_3$$$ $$$\dots$$$ $$$w_n$$$`" ($$$0 \leq w_i \lt 2^{30}$$$). After flushing your output, your program should exit immediately.



Note that the answer for each test case is pre-determined. That is, the interactor is not adaptive. Also, note that your guess does not count as a query.



To flush your output, you can use:



- `fflush(stdout)` (if you use `printf`) or `cout.flush()` (if you use `cout`) in C and C++.

- `System.out.flush()` in Java and Kotlin.

- `stdout.flush()` in Python.

# Horizon Scanning

Cold joke: Radar is a palindrome.

Explanation: It's actually cold knowledge, not a cold joke. The confusion between these concepts is what makes it funny.



—Soy-chicken



Hana recently needs to develop a radar system to monitor abnormal activities across the archipelago she manages.



There are $$$n$$$ islands in the ocean, and the $$$i$$$-th island is located at coordinates $$$(x_i, y_i)$$$, which can be treated as a point on the plane. Assume the radar has a scanning angle range of $$$\alpha$$$. When the radar is rotated to an angle $$$\theta$$$, it can monitor all the islands located within the angular range $$$[\theta - \frac{\alpha}{2}, \theta + \frac{\alpha}{2}]$$$.



Hana is currently low on funds, so she wants to minimize the cost of building the radar. She wants to know, when the radar is placed at the origin $$$(0,0)$$$, what the minimum scanning angle $$$\alpha$$$ should be to ensure that for any angle $$$\theta$$$, the radar can monitor at least $$$k$$$ islands.



## Input



Each test file contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$T$$$ ($$$1 \leq T \leq 10^4$$$). The description of each test case follows.



The first line of each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \leq k \leq n \leq 2 \times 10^5$$$), representing the total number of islands and the minimum number of islands the radar must monitor at any given time.



The next $$$n$$$ lines each contain two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$|x_i|, |y_i| \leq 10^9$$$), representing the position of an island. It is guaranteed that the coordinates of any two islands are different and none of them are located at the origin.



For each test file, it is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \times 10^5$$$.



## Output



For each test case, output a single decimal fraction representing the minimum radar scanning angle in radians.



Your answer is considered correct if its absolute or relative error does not exceed $$$10^{-6}$$$.



Formally, let your answer be $$$a$$$, and the jury's answer be $$$b$$$. Your answer is accepted if and only if $$$\frac{|a - b|}{\max{(1, |b|)}} \leq 10^{-6}$$$.



## Note



For the first test case in the example, there is only one island on the plane at $$$(0,1)$$$. To ensure that at least one island is always within range, the radar's monitoring range must be set to $$$360^{\circ}$$$, which is $$$2 \pi$$$ in radians.



For the second test case in the example, there are $$$8$$$ islands on the plane, with each pair of islands separated by $$$45^{\circ}$$$. If the radar's range is less than $$$90^{\circ}$$$, it would only be able to monitor one island when one of its boundaries just moves past an island (as shown on the left of the illustration). Therefore, the minimum radar range needed is $$$90^{\circ}$$$, ensuring that at least two islands are always within range.

# Just another Sorting Problem

According to the problem statement, Bob is the one who lives longer.



—Hotpot-chicken



Jessica is a master of sorting algorithms, proficient in selection sort, insertion sort, bubble sort, and many others. Therefore, she decided to host a sorting competition.



The competition takes place on a permutation$$$^{\dagger}$$$ $$$p$$$ of length $$$n$$$, with two participants: Alice and Bob. The two players take turns performing operations, with the first player being decided by a coin toss. If the sequence is in ascending order after any player's turn, Alice wins immediately. If Alice cannot win within a finite number of turns, Bob is considered the winner.



On Alice's turn, she can choose any two positions $$$i,j$$$ ($$$i \neq j, 1 \leq i,j \leq n$$$) in the permutation and swap $$$p_i$$$ and $$$p_j$$$. On Bob's turn, he can select two adjacent positions $$$i,i+1$$$ ($$$1 \leq i \lt n$$$) and swap $$$p_i$$$ and $$$p_{i+1}$$$. Neither player is allowed to skip their turn.



Given the permutation $$$p$$$ and the name of the player who operates first, determine who will win the game if both players play optimally.



$$$^{\dagger}$$$ A permutation of length $$$n$$$ is an array consisting of $$$n$$$ distinct integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ in arbitrary order. For example, $$$[2,3,1,5,4]$$$ is a permutation, but $$$[1,2,2]$$$ is not a permutation ($$$2$$$ appears twice in the array), and $$$[1,3,4]$$$ is also not a permutation ($$$n=3$$$ but there is a $$$4$$$ in the array).



## Input



Each test file contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$T$$$ ($$$1 \leq T \leq 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows.



The first line of each test case contains an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \leq n \leq 10^5$$$) and a string $$$s$$$ ($$$s \in \{$$$`Alice`, `Bob`$$$\}$$$), representing the length of the permutation and the name of the player who operates first.



The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$p_1, p_2, \cdots, p_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq p_i \leq n$$$), representing the permutation $$$p$$$. It is guaranteed that there is at least one position $$$i$$$ such that $$$p_i \neq i$$$.



For each test file, it is guaranteed that the sum of all $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^5$$$.



## Output



For each test case, output one line containing the winner's name. If Alice wins, print "`Alice`"; otherwise, print "`Bob`".
