# Drink

Some unexpected incidents occurred during the village chief election. Due to Xiaochang and Xiaopeng violating election rules and being disqualified, Xiao Ming was ultimately elected as the new village chief. As a result, Xiao Ming decided to treat everyone to a meal together.

In Zhangjia Village, the local customs are quite bold; meals must involve drinking wine and playing a game called "Drink to the Finish".

To describe this game specifically: $$$n$$$ people sit in a circle, and the $$$i$$$-th person holds a die that can roll an integer between $$$[1,a_i]$$$ with equal probability.

The game proceeds in rounds. At the start of each round:

(1) All people who have not yet become "wine dazed" roll their dice once.

(2) Now, each person checks the numbers rolled by their left and right neighbors. Assuming their own rolled number is $$$x$$$, and their left and right neighbors' numbers are $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ respectively, then in this round they need to drink $$$\max(0,a-x)+\max(0,b-x)$$$ grams of wine.

(3) Those who roll $$$x=1$$$ in this round will become "wine dazed" and can no longer roll their dice. Their number is fixed at 1 thereafter.

(4) The game ends when everyone has become "wine dazed".

Xiao Ming is worried that everyone might drink too much, but also wants to know whether his wine tolerance can last until the game ends. So he asks you to calculate: In this game, how many grams of wine is each person expected to drink?

## Input

The first line contains an integer $$$n$$$, representing the number of participants in the game.

The second line contains $$$n$$$ positive integers $$$a_1,\ldots,a_n$$$, listed clockwise to represent the parameters of each participant's die.

$$$3 \le n \le 10^5$$$

$$$1 \le a_i \le 10^5$$$

## Output

Output one line containing $$$n$$$ integers, representing the expected amount of wine each person $$$1,2,\ldots,n$$$ will drink respectively.

It can be proved that each answer can be expressed as a fraction $$$\frac{x}{y}$$$ ($$$\gcd(x,y)=1$$$). You only need to output $$$x \times y^{-1} \bmod 998244353$$$, where $$$y^{-1}$$$ is the unique integer satisfying $$$0 \lt y^{-1} \lt 998244353$$$ and $$$y \times y^{-1} \bmod 998244353 = 1$$$.

## Note

Clearly, the 3rd person won't drink any wine, while the 1st and 2nd persons drink equivalent amounts. All possible scenarios are:

$$$\frac{1}{2}$$$: $$$[1]$$$ – The game ends immediately (the left fraction represents probability).

$$$\frac{1}{4}$$$: $$$[2,1]$$$ – The 1st and 2nd persons need to drink $$$2-1=1$$$ unit of wine.

$$$\frac{1}{8}$$$: $$$[2,2,1]$$$ – The 1st and 2nd persons need to drink $$$2 \times (2-1)=2$$$ units of wine.

$$$\frac{1}{16}$$$: $$$[2,2,2,1]$$$ – The 1st and 2nd persons need to drink $$$3 \times (2-1)=3$$$ units of wine.

...

The answer can be easily calculated as $$$1 \times \frac{1}{4}+2 \times \frac{1}{8}+3 \times \frac{1}{16}+\ldots=1$$$.

# Drink

村长选举出现了一些意外情况。由于小昌和小鹏违反选举规则被取消资格，小明最终当选为新村长。于是小明决定请大家一起吃顿饭。

在张家村，当地风俗相当豪放；吃饭必须喝酒，还要玩一个叫“喝到底”的游戏。

具体描述这个游戏：$$$n$$$个人围坐成一圈，第$$$i$$$个人拿着一个骰子，可以等概率掷出$$$[1,a_i]$$$之间的整数。

游戏按轮进行。每轮开始时：

(1) 所有尚未“醉倒”的人掷一次自己的骰子。

(2) 现在，每个人查看自己左右邻居掷出的数字。假设自己掷出的数字是$$$x$$$，左右邻居的数字分别是$$$a$$$和$$$b$$$，那么这一轮他们需要喝$$$\max(0,a-x)+\max(0,b-x)$$$克酒。

(3) 这一轮掷出$$$x=1$$$的人会变成“醉倒”状态，不能再掷骰子。此后他们的数字固定为1。

(4) 当所有人都“醉倒”时，游戏结束。

小明担心大家可能喝得太多，但也想知道自己的酒量能否撑到游戏结束。于是他请你计算：在这个游戏中，每个人期望喝多少克酒？

## 输入

第一行包含一个整数$$$n$$$，表示游戏参与人数。

第二行包含$$$n$$$个正整数$$$a_1,\ldots,a_n$$$，按顺时针顺序列出，表示每个参与者骰子的参数。

$$$3 \le n \le 10^5$$$

$$$1 \le a_i \le 10^5$$$

## 输出

输出一行，包含$$$n$$$个整数，分别表示每个人$$$1,2,\ldots,n$$$期望喝的酒量。

可以证明，每个答案都可以表示为一个分数$$$\frac{x}{y}$$$（$$$\gcd(x,y)=1$$$）。你只需要输出$$$x \times y^{-1} \bmod 998244353$$$，其中$$$y^{-1}$$$是满足$$$0 \lt y^{-1} \lt 998244353$$$和$$$y \times y^{-1} \bmod 998244353 = 1$$$的唯一整数。

## 说明

显然，第3个人不会喝任何酒，而第1个人和第2个人喝的量相同。所有可能的情况是：

$$$\frac{1}{2}$$$：$$$[1]$$$——游戏立即结束（左侧分数表示概率）。

$$$\frac{1}{4}$$$：$$$[2,1]$$$ —— 第 1 个人和第 2 个人需要喝 $$$2-1=1$$$ 单位酒。

$$$\frac{1}{8}$$$：$$$[2,2,1]$$$ —— 第 1 个人和第 2 个人需要喝 $$$2 \times (2-1)=2$$$ 单位酒。

$$$\frac{1}{16}$$$：$$$[2,2,2,1]$$$ —— 第 1 个人和第 2 个人需要喝 $$$3 \times (2-1)=3$$$ 单位酒。

...

答案可以很容易地计算为 $$$1 \times \frac{1}{4}+2 \times \frac{1}{8}+3 \times \frac{1}{16}+\ldots=1$$$。

# Juan

Xiaochang and Xiaopeng are preparing for the postgraduate entrance exam together, sitting back-to-back in the study room day after day.

Originally, Xiaochang was better at studying than Xiaopeng, so he doesn't want Xiaopeng to surpass him. Xiaopeng is very hardworking himself, but he doesn't want Xiaochang to see him working too hard.

Specifically:

- Xiaochang has a sequence $$$A$$$ of length $$$n$$$, where the $$$i$$$-th position ($$$0 \le i \lt n$$$) $$$A_i$$$ is either 1 or 0, representing whether he looks back to check if Xiaopeng is working hard (1) or not (0).

- Xiaopeng has a sequence $$$B$$$ of length $$$m$$$, where the $$$j$$$-th position ($$$0 \le j \lt m$$$) $$$B_j$$$ is either 1 or 0, representing whether he is working hard (1) or playing with his phone (0) at that moment.

Over the next $$$n \times m$$$ days, at 11:00 am on the $$$k$$$-th day ($$$0 \le k \lt n \times m$$$):

- If $$$A_{k \bmod n}=1$$$, Xiaochang will look back at Xiaopeng; otherwise, he won't.

- If $$$B_{k \bmod m}=1$$$, Xiaopeng will be working hard at that moment; otherwise, he will be playing with his phone.

The trust level of Xiaochang towards Xiaopeng increases by 1 in the following two cases:

- Xiaochang looks back and sees Xiaopeng playing.

- Xiaochang doesn't look back, but Xiaopeng is working hard.

Given $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, and Xiaochang's sequences, the question is: Assuming Xiaopeng constructs his sequence in the optimal way, what is the maximum trust level Xiaochang can have towards Xiaopeng after $$$n \times m$$$ days?

## Input

The first line contains two positive integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$, as described in the problem statement.

The second line contains a binary string of length $$$n$$$, representing Xiaochang's sequence $$$A$$$.

$$$1 \le n,m \le 10^5$$$

## Output

Output a single number representing the answer.

## Note

For the first sample case, Xiaopeng can set his sequence to 0000, so whenever Xiaochang looks back, Xiaopeng is playing, resulting in the answer $$$n \times m=3 \times 4=12$$$.

For the second sample case, during these 6 days, Xiaopeng's observation sequence is 101101, while Xiaochang's sequence expands to $$$B_0B_1B_0B_1B_0B_1$$$.

Each day's decisions correspond to: $$$\{1,B_0\}$$$, $$$\{0,B_1\}$$$, $$$\{1,B_0\}$$$, $$$\{1,B_1\}$$$, $$$\{0,B_0\}$$$, $$$\{1,B_1\}$$$.

It's easy to see that setting $$$B_0=B_1=0$$$ yields the maximum answer of 4.

# Vasya and Robot

Vasya has got a robot which is situated on an infinite Cartesian plane, initially in the cell $$$(0, 0)$$$. Robot can perform the following four kinds of operations:

- `U` — move from $$$(x, y)$$$ to $$$(x, y + 1)$$$;

- `D` — move from $$$(x, y)$$$ to $$$(x, y - 1)$$$;

- `L` — move from $$$(x, y)$$$ to $$$(x - 1, y)$$$;

- `R` — move from $$$(x, y)$$$ to $$$(x + 1, y)$$$.

Vasya also has got a sequence of $$$n$$$ operations. Vasya wants to modify this sequence so after performing it the robot will end up in $$$(x, y)$$$.

Vasya wants to change the sequence so the length of changed subsegment is minimum possible. This length can be calculated as follows: $$$maxID - minID + 1$$$, where $$$maxID$$$ is the maximum index of a changed operation, and $$$minID$$$ is the minimum index of a changed operation. For example, if Vasya changes `RRRRRRR` to `RLRRLRL`, then the operations with indices $$$2$$$, $$$5$$$ and $$$7$$$ are changed, so the length of changed subsegment is $$$7 - 2 + 1 = 6$$$. Another example: if Vasya changes `DDDD` to `DDRD`, then the length of changed subsegment is $$$1$$$.

If there are no changes, then the length of changed subsegment is $$$0$$$. Changing an operation means replacing it with some operation (possibly the same); Vasya can't insert new operations into the sequence or remove them.

Help Vasya! Tell him the minimum length of subsegment that he needs to change so that the robot will go from $$$(0, 0)$$$ to $$$(x, y)$$$, or tell him that it's impossible.

## Input

The first line contains one integer number $$$n~(1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5)$$$ — the number of operations.

The second line contains the sequence of operations — a string of $$$n$$$ characters. Each character is either `U`, `D`, `L` or `R`.

The third line contains two integers $$$x, y~(-10^9 \le x, y \le 10^9)$$$ — the coordinates of the cell where the robot should end its path.

## Output

Print one integer — the minimum possible length of subsegment that can be changed so the resulting sequence of operations moves the robot from $$$(0, 0)$$$ to $$$(x, y)$$$. If this change is impossible, print $$$-1$$$.

## Note

In the first example the sequence can be changed to `LULUU`. So the length of the changed subsegment is $$$3 - 1 + 1 = 3$$$.

In the second example the given sequence already leads the robot to $$$(x, y)$$$, so the length of the changed subsegment is $$$0$$$.

In the third example the robot can't end his path in the cell $$$(x, y)$$$.

# Choosing Two Paths

You are given an undirected unweighted tree consisting of $$$n$$$ vertices.

An undirected tree is a connected undirected graph with $$$n - 1$$$ edges.

Your task is to choose two pairs of vertices of this tree (all the chosen vertices should be distinct) $$$(x_1, y_1)$$$ and $$$(x_2, y_2)$$$ in such a way that neither $$$x_1$$$ nor $$$y_1$$$ belong to the simple path from $$$x_2$$$ to $$$y_2$$$ and vice versa (neither $$$x_2$$$ nor $$$y_2$$$ should not belong to the simple path from $$$x_1$$$ to $$$y_1$$$).

It is guaranteed that it is possible to choose such pairs for the given tree.

Among all possible ways to choose such pairs you have to choose one with the maximum number of common vertices between paths from $$$x_1$$$ to $$$y_1$$$ and from $$$x_2$$$ to $$$y_2$$$. And among all such pairs you have to choose one with the maximum total length of these two paths.

It is guaranteed that the answer with at least two common vertices exists for the given tree.

The length of the path is the number of edges in it.

The simple path is the path that visits each vertex at most once.

## Input

The first line contains an integer $$$n$$$ — the number of vertices in the tree ($$$6 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$).

Each of the next $$$n - 1$$$ lines describes the edges of the tree.

Edge $$$i$$$ is denoted by two integers $$$u_i$$$ and $$$v_i$$$, the labels of vertices it connects ($$$1 \le u_i, v_i \le n$$$, $$$u_i \ne v_i$$$).

It is guaranteed that the given edges form a tree.

It is guaranteed that the answer with at least two common vertices exists for the given tree.

## Output

Print any two pairs of vertices satisfying the conditions described in the problem statement.

It is guaranteed that it is possible to choose such pairs for the given tree.

## Note

The picture corresponding to the first example: ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/061b9a7f2795fb8fd95c5b77fadee6b5d68421e7.png)

The intersection of two paths is $$$2$$$ (vertices $$$1$$$ and $$$4$$$) and the total length is $$$4 + 3 = 7$$$.

The intersection of two paths is $$$2$$$ (vertices $$$3$$$ and $$$4$$$) and the total length is $$$5 + 3 = 8$$$.

The intersection of two paths is $$$3$$$ (vertices $$$2$$$, $$$7$$$ and $$$8$$$) and the total length is $$$5 + 5 = 10$$$.

The picture corresponding to the fourth example: ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/aa7bd6634ff1c9a3efe0c237841d1f57c9d16de1.png)

The intersection of two paths is $$$5$$$ (vertices $$$1$$$, $$$2$$$, $$$3$$$, $$$4$$$ and $$$5$$$) and the total length is $$$6 + 6 = 12$$$.

# Yet Another LCP Problem

Let $$$\text{LCP}(s, t)$$$ be the length of the longest common prefix of strings $$$s$$$ and $$$t$$$. Also let $$$s[x \dots y]$$$ be the substring of $$$s$$$ from index $$$x$$$ to index $$$y$$$ (inclusive). For example, if $$$s = $$$ "`abcde`", then $$$s[1 \dots 3] =$$$ "`abc`", $$$s[2 \dots 5] =$$$ "`bcde`".

You are given a string $$$s$$$ of length $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ queries. Each query is a pair of integer sets $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_k$$$ and $$$b_1, b_2, \dots, b_l$$$. Calculate $$$\sum\limits_{i = 1}^{i = k} \sum\limits_{j = 1}^{j = l}{\text{LCP}(s[a_i \dots n], s[b_j \dots n])}$$$ for each query.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le n, q \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the length of string $$$s$$$ and the number of queries, respectively.

The second line contains a string $$$s$$$ consisting of lowercase Latin letters ($$$|s| = n$$$).

Next $$$3q$$$ lines contains descriptions of queries — three lines per query. The first line of each query contains two integers $$$k_i$$$ and $$$l_i$$$ ($$$1 \le k_i, l_i \le n$$$) — sizes of sets $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ respectively.

The second line of each query contains $$$k_i$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots a_{k_i}$$$ ($$$1 \le a_1 \lt a_2 \lt \dots \lt a_{k_i} \le n$$$) — set $$$a$$$.

The third line of each query contains $$$l_i$$$ integers $$$b_1, b_2, \dots b_{l_i}$$$ ($$$1 \le b_1 \lt b_2 \lt \dots \lt b_{l_i} \le n$$$) — set $$$b$$$.

It is guaranteed that $$$\sum\limits_{i = 1}^{i = q}{k_i} \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$ and $$$\sum\limits_{i = 1}^{i = q}{l_i} \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$.

## Output

Print $$$q$$$ integers — answers for the queries in the same order queries are given in the input.

## Note

Description of queries:

- In the first query $$$s[1 \dots 7] = \text{abacaba}$$$ and $$$s[2 \dots 7] = \text{bacaba}$$$ are considered. The answer for the query is $$$\text{LCP}(\text{abacaba}, \text{abacaba}) + \text{LCP}(\text{abacaba}, \text{bacaba}) + \text{LCP}(\text{bacaba}, \text{abacaba}) + \text{LCP}(\text{bacaba}, \text{bacaba}) = 7 + 0 + 0 + 6 = 13$$$.

- In the second query $$$s[1 \dots 7] = \text{abacaba}$$$, $$$s[2 \dots 7] = \text{bacaba}$$$, $$$s[3 \dots 7] = \text{acaba}$$$ and $$$s[7 \dots 7] = \text{a}$$$ are considered. The answer for the query is $$$\text{LCP}(\text{abacaba}, \text{a}) + \text{LCP}(\text{bacaba}, \text{a}) + \text{LCP}(\text{acaba}, \text{a}) = 1 + 0 + 1 = 2$$$.

- In the third query $$$s[1 \dots 7] = \text{abacaba}$$$ are compared with all suffixes. The answer is the sum of non-zero values: $$$\text{LCP}(\text{abacaba}, \text{abacaba}) + \text{LCP}(\text{abacaba}, \text{acaba}) + \text{LCP}(\text{abacaba}, \text{aba}) + \text{LCP}(\text{abacaba}, \text{a}) = 7 + 1 + 3 + 1 = 12$$$.

- In the fourth query $$$s[1 \dots 7] = \text{abacaba}$$$ and $$$s[5 \dots 7] = \text{aba}$$$ are considered. The answer for the query is $$$\text{LCP}(\text{abacaba}, \text{abacaba}) + \text{LCP}(\text{abacaba}, \text{aba}) + \text{LCP}(\text{aba}, \text{abacaba}) + \text{LCP}(\text{aba}, \text{aba}) = 7 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 16$$$.

设 $$$\text{LCP}(s, t)$$$ 为字符串 $$$s$$$ 和 $$$t$$$ 的最长公共前缀的长度。同时设 $$$s[x \dots y]$$$ 为 $$$s$$$ 中从下标 $$$x$$$ 到下标 $$$y$$$（包含两端）的子串。例如，如果 $$$s = $$$ "`abcde`"，那么 $$$s[1 \dots 3] =$$$ "`abc`"，$$$s[2 \dots 5] =$$$ "`bcde`"。

第二行包含一个由小写拉丁字母组成的字符串 $$$s$$$（$$$|s| = n$$$）。





接下来 $$$3q$$$ 行包含询问的描述 —— 每个询问三行。每个询问的第一行包含两个整数 $$$k_i$$$ 和 $$$l_i$$$（$$$1 \le k_i, l_i \le n$$$）—— 分别为集合 $$$a$$$ 和 $$$b$$$ 的大小。





每个询问的第二行包含 $$$k_i$$$ 个整数 $$$a_1, a_2, \dots a_{k_i}$$$（$$$1 \le a_1 \lt a_2 \lt \dots \lt a_{k_i} \le n$$$）—— 集合 $$$a$$$。





每个询问的第三行包含 $$$l_i$$$ 个整数 $$$b_1, b_2, \dots b_{l_i}$$$（$$$1 \le b_1 \lt b_2 \lt \dots \lt b_{l_i} \le n$$$）—— 集合 $$$b$$$。





保证 $$$\sum\limits_{i = 1}^{i = q}{k_i} \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$ 且 $$$\sum\limits_{i = 1}^{i = q}{l_i} \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$。





## 输出





输出 $$$q$$$ 个整数 —— 按照输入中询问给出的顺序，每个询问的答案。





## 说明





询问的描述：





- 在第一个询问中，考虑了 $$$s[1 \dots 7] = \text{abacaba}$$$ 和 $$$s[2 \dots 7] = \text{bacaba}$$$。该询问的答案为 $$$\text{LCP}(\text{abacaba}, \text{abacaba}) + \text{LCP}(\text{abacaba}, \text{bacaba}) + \text{LCP}(\text{bacaba}, \text{abacaba}) + \text{LCP}(\text{bacaba}, \text{bacaba}) = 7 + 0 + 0 + 6 = 13$$$。





- 在第二个询问中，考虑了 $$$s[1 \dots 7] = \text{abacaba}$$$、$$$s[2 \dots 7] = \text{bacaba}$$$、$$$s[3 \dots 7] = \text{acaba}$$$ 和 $$$s[7 \dots 7] = \text{a}$$$。该询问的答案为 $$$\text{LCP}(\text{abacaba}, \text{a}) + \text{LCP}(\text{bacaba}, \text{a}) + \text{LCP}(\text{acaba}, \text{a}) = 1 + 0 + 1 = 2$$$。





- 在第三个询问中，将 $$$s[1 \dots 7] = \text{abacaba}$$$ 与所有后缀进行比较。答案为非零值之和：$$$\text{LCP}(\text{abacaba}, \text{abacaba}) + \text{LCP}(\text{abacaba}, \text{acaba}) + \text{LCP}(\text{abacaba}, \text{aba}) + \text{LCP}(\text{abacaba}, \text{a}) = 7 + 1 + 3 + 1 = 12$$$。





- 在第四个询问中，考虑了 $$$s[1 \dots 7] = \text{abacaba}$$$ 和 $$$s[5 \dots 7] = \text{aba}$$$。该询问的答案为 $$$\text{LCP}(\text{abacaba}, \text{abacaba}) + \text{LCP}(\text{abacaba}, \text{aba}) + \text{LCP}(\text{aba}, \text{abacaba}) + \text{LCP}(\text{aba}, \text{aba}) = 7 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 16$$$。

# Summer Practice Report

Vova has taken his summer practice this year and now he should write a report on how it went.

Vova has already drawn all the tables and wrote down all the formulas. Moreover, he has already decided that the report will consist of exactly $$$n$$$ pages and the $$$i$$$-th page will include $$$x_i$$$ tables and $$$y_i$$$ formulas. The pages are numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$.

Vova fills the pages one after another, he can't go filling page $$$i + 1$$$ before finishing page $$$i$$$ and he can't skip pages.

However, if he draws strictly more than $$$k$$$ tables in a row or writes strictly more than $$$k$$$ formulas in a row then he will get bored. Vova wants to rearrange tables and formulas in each page in such a way that he doesn't get bored in the process. Vova can't move some table or some formula to another page.

Note that the count doesn't reset on the start of the new page. For example, if the page ends with $$$3$$$ tables and the next page starts with $$$5$$$ tables, then it's counted as $$$8$$$ tables in a row.

Help Vova to determine if he can rearrange tables and formulas on each page in such a way that there is no more than $$$k$$$ tables in a row and no more than $$$k$$$ formulas in a row.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$, $$$1 \le k \le 10^6$$$).

The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i \le 10^6$$$) — the number of tables on the $$$i$$$-th page.

The third line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$y_1, y_2, \dots, y_n$$$ ($$$1 \le y_i \le 10^6$$$) — the number of formulas on the $$$i$$$-th page.

## Output

Print "`YES`" if Vova can rearrange tables and formulas on each page in such a way that there is no more than $$$k$$$ tables in a row and no more than $$$k$$$ formulas in a row.

Otherwise print "`NO`".

## Note

In the first example the only option to rearrange everything is the following (let table be '`T`' and formula be '`F`'):

- page $$$1$$$: "`TTFTTFT`"

- page $$$2$$$: "`TFTTFTT`"

That way all blocks of tables have length $$$2$$$.

In the second example there is no way to fit everything in such a way that there are no more than $$$2$$$ tables in a row and $$$2$$$ formulas in a row.

# The Top Scorer

Hasan loves playing games and has recently discovered a game called TopScore. In this soccer-like game there are $$$p$$$ players doing penalty shoot-outs. Winner is the one who scores the most. In case of ties, one of the top-scorers will be declared as the winner randomly with equal probability.

They have just finished the game and now are waiting for the result. But there's a tiny problem! The judges have lost the paper of scores! Fortunately they have calculated sum of the scores before they get lost and also for some of the players they have remembered a lower bound on how much they scored. However, the information about the bounds is private, so Hasan only got to know his bound.

According to the available data, he knows that his score is at least $$$r$$$ and sum of the scores is $$$s$$$.

Thus the final state of the game can be represented in form of sequence of $$$p$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_p$$$ ($$$0 \le a_i$$$) — player's scores. Hasan is player number $$$1$$$, so $$$a_1 \ge r$$$. Also $$$a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_p = s$$$. Two states are considered different if there exists some position $$$i$$$ such that the value of $$$a_i$$$ differs in these states.

Once again, Hasan doesn't know the exact scores (he doesn't know his exact score as well). So he considers each of the final states to be equally probable to achieve.

Help Hasan find the probability of him winning.

It can be shown that it is in the form of $$$\frac{P}{Q}$$$ where $$$P$$$ and $$$Q$$$ are non-negative integers and $$$Q \ne 0$$$, $$$P \le Q$$$. Report the value of $$$P \cdot Q^{-1} \pmod {998244353}$$$.

## Input

The only line contains three integers $$$p$$$, $$$s$$$ and $$$r$$$ ($$$1 \le p \le 100$$$, $$$0 \le r \le s \le 5000$$$) — the number of players, the sum of scores of all players and Hasan's score, respectively.

## Output

Print a single integer — the probability of Hasan winning.

It can be shown that it is in the form of $$$\frac{P}{Q}$$$ where $$$P$$$ and $$$Q$$$ are non-negative integers and $$$Q \ne 0$$$, $$$P \le Q$$$. Report the value of $$$P \cdot Q^{-1} \pmod {998244353}$$$.

## Note

In the first example Hasan can score $$$3$$$, $$$4$$$, $$$5$$$ or $$$6$$$ goals. If he scores $$$4$$$ goals or more than he scores strictly more than his only opponent. If he scores $$$3$$$ then his opponent also scores $$$3$$$ and Hasan has a probability of $$$\frac 1 2$$$ to win the game. Thus, overall he has the probability of $$$\frac 7 8$$$ to win.

In the second example even Hasan's lower bound on goal implies him scoring more than any of his opponents. Thus, the resulting probability is $$$1$$$.
content.title: The Top Scorer

# Polycarp's New Job

Polycarp has recently got himself a new job. He now earns so much that his old wallet can't even store all the money he has.

Berland bills somehow come in lots of different sizes. However, all of them are shaped as rectangles (possibly squares). All wallets are also produced in form of rectangles (possibly squares).

A bill $$$x \times y$$$ fits into some wallet $$$h \times w$$$ if either $$$x \le h$$$ and $$$y \le w$$$ or $$$y \le h$$$ and $$$x \le w$$$. Bills can overlap with each other in a wallet and an infinite amount of bills can fit into a wallet. That implies that all the bills Polycarp currently have fit into a wallet if every single one of them fits into it independently of the others.

Now you are asked to perform the queries of two types:

- $$$+~x~y$$$ — Polycarp earns a bill of size $$$x \times y$$$;

- $$$?~h~w$$$ — Polycarp wants to check if all the bills he has earned to this moment fit into a wallet of size $$$h \times w$$$.

It is guaranteed that there is at least one query of type $$$1$$$ before the first query of type $$$2$$$ and that there is at least one query of type $$$2$$$ in the input data.

For each query of type $$$2$$$ print "`YES`" if all the bills he has earned to this moment fit into a wallet of given size. Print "`NO`" otherwise.

## Input

The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 5 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of queries.

Each of the next $$$n$$$ lines contains a query of one of these two types:

- $$$+~x~y$$$ ($$$1 \le x, y \le 10^9$$$) — Polycarp earns a bill of size $$$x \times y$$$;

- $$$?~h~w$$$ ($$$1 \le h, w \le 10^9$$$) — Polycarp wants to check if all the bills he has earned to this moment fit into a wallet of size $$$h \times w$$$.

It is guaranteed that there is at least one query of type $$$1$$$ before the first query of type $$$2$$$ and that there is at least one query of type $$$2$$$ in the input data.

## Output

For each query of type $$$2$$$ print "`YES`" if all the bills he has earned to this moment fit into a wallet of given size. Print "`NO`" otherwise.

## Note

The queries of type $$$2$$$ of the example:

- Neither bill fits;

- Both bills fit (just checking that you got that bills can overlap);

- Both bills fit (both bills are actually the same);

- All bills fit (too much of free space in a wallet is not a problem);

- Only bill $$$1 \times 5$$$ fit (all the others don't, thus it's "`NO`").
content.title: Polycarp's New Job

# Polycarp 的新工作

Polycarp 最近给自己找了一份新工作。他现在赚得太多，以至于他的旧钱包甚至装不下他所有的钱。

现在要求你执行两种类型的查询：

- $$$+~x~y$$$ —— Polycarp 赚到一张尺寸为 $$$x \times y$$$ 的钞票；

- $$$?~h~w$$$ —— Polycarp 想检查他到此刻为止赚到的所有钞票是否都能放进一个尺寸为 $$$h \times w$$$ 的钱包。

保证在第一个类型 $$$2$$$ 的查询之前至少有一个类型 $$$1$$$ 的查询，并且输入数据中至少有一个类型 $$$2$$$ 的查询。

对于每个类型 $$$2$$$ 的查询，如果到此刻为止他赚到的所有钞票都能放进给定尺寸的钱包，则输出 "`YES`"，否则输出 "`NO`"。

第一行包含一个整数 $$$n$$$（$$$2 \le n \le 5 \cdot 10^5$$$）—— 查询的数量。

接下来的 $$$n$$$ 行中，每行包含以下两种类型之一的查询：

- $$$+~x~y$$$（$$$1 \le x, y \le 10^9$$$）—— Polycarp 赚到一张尺寸为 $$$x \times y$$$ 的钞票；

- $$$?~h~w$$$（$$$1 \le h, w \le 10^9$$$）—— Polycarp 想检查他到此刻为止赚到的所有钞票是否都能放进一个尺寸为 $$$h \times w$$$ 的钱包。

保证在第一个类型 $$$2$$$ 的查询之前至少有一个类型 $$$1$$$ 的查询，并且输入数据中至少有一个类型 $$$2$$$ 的查询。

对于每个类型 $$$2$$$ 的查询，如果到此刻为止他赚到的所有钞票都能放进给定尺寸的钱包，则输出 "`YES`"，否则输出 "`NO`"。

## 说明

示例中类型 $$$2$$$ 的查询：

- 所有钞票都放得下（钱包里空余空间太多不是问题）；

# Trucks and Cities

There are $$$n$$$ cities along the road, which can be represented as a straight line. The $$$i$$$-th city is situated at the distance of $$$a_i$$$ kilometers from the origin. All cities are situated in the same direction from the origin. There are $$$m$$$ trucks travelling from one city to another.

Each truck can be described by $$$4$$$ integers: starting city $$$s_i$$$, finishing city $$$f_i$$$, fuel consumption $$$c_i$$$ and number of possible refuelings $$$r_i$$$. The $$$i$$$-th truck will spend $$$c_i$$$ litres of fuel per one kilometer.

When a truck arrives in some city, it can be refueled (but refueling is impossible in the middle of nowhere). The $$$i$$$-th truck can be refueled at most $$$r_i$$$ times. Each refueling makes truck's gas-tank full. All trucks start with full gas-tank.

All trucks will have gas-tanks of the same size $$$V$$$ litres. You should find minimum possible $$$V$$$ such that all trucks can reach their destinations without refueling more times than allowed.

## Input

First line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 400$$$, $$$1 \le m \le 250000$$$) — the number of cities and trucks.

The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$, $$$a_i \lt a_{i+1}$$$) — positions of cities in the ascending order.

Next $$$m$$$ lines contains $$$4$$$ integers each. The $$$i$$$-th line contains integers $$$s_i$$$, $$$f_i$$$, $$$c_i$$$, $$$r_i$$$ ($$$1 \le s_i \lt f_i \le n$$$, $$$1 \le c_i \le 10^9$$$, $$$0 \le r_i \le n$$$) — the description of the $$$i$$$-th truck.

## Output

Print the only integer — minimum possible size of gas-tanks $$$V$$$ such that all trucks can reach their destinations.

## Note

Let's look at queries in details:

- the $$$1$$$-st truck must arrive at position $$$7$$$ from $$$2$$$ without refuelling, so it needs gas-tank of volume at least $$$50$$$.

- the $$$2$$$-nd truck must arrive at position $$$17$$$ from $$$2$$$ and can be refueled at any city (if it is on the path between starting point and ending point), so it needs gas-tank of volume at least $$$48$$$.

- the $$$3$$$-rd truck must arrive at position $$$14$$$ from $$$10$$$, there is no city between, so it needs gas-tank of volume at least $$$52$$$.

- the $$$4$$$-th truck must arrive at position $$$17$$$ from $$$10$$$ and can be refueled only one time: it's optimal to refuel at $$$5$$$-th city (position $$$14$$$) so it needs gas-tank of volume at least $$$40$$$.

- the $$$5$$$-th truck has the same description, so it also needs gas-tank of volume at least $$$40$$$.

- the $$$6$$$-th truck must arrive at position $$$14$$$ from $$$2$$$ and can be refueled two times: first time in city $$$2$$$ or $$$3$$$ and second time in city $$$4$$$ so it needs gas-tank of volume at least $$$55$$$.

# 卡车与城市

沿着道路有$$$n$$$座城市，可以将它们表示为一条直线。第$$$i$$$座城市位于距原点$$$a_i$$$千米处。所有城市都位于原点的同一方向。有$$$m$$$辆卡车从一座城市前往另一座城市。

每辆卡车可以用$$$4$$$个整数描述：起始城市$$$s_i$$$、终点城市$$$f_i$$$、燃料消耗$$$c_i$$$以及可能的加油次数$$$r_i$$$。第$$$i$$$辆卡车每行驶一千米将消耗$$$c_i$$$升燃料。

当卡车到达某座城市时，它可以加油（但不能在荒郊野外加油）。第$$$i$$$辆卡车最多可以加油$$$r_i$$$次。每次加油都会使卡车的油箱加满。所有卡车出发时油箱都是满的。

所有卡车的油箱容量都相同，为$$$V$$$升。你需要求出最小的可能$$$V$$$，使得所有卡车都能在不超过允许加油次数的情况下到达目的地。

## 输入

第一行包含两个整数$$$n$$$和$$$m$$$（$$$2 \le n \le 400$$$，$$$1 \le m \le 250000$$$）——城市数量和卡车数量。

第二行包含$$$n$$$个整数$$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$（$$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$，$$$a_i \lt a_{i+1}$$$）——按升序给出的城市位置。

接下来$$$m$$$行每行包含$$$4$$$个整数。第$$$i$$$行包含整数$$$s_i$$$、$$$f_i$$$、$$$c_i$$$、$$$r_i$$$（$$$1 \le s_i \lt f_i \le n$$$，$$$1 \le c_i \le 10^9$$$，$$$0 \le r_i \le n$$$）——第$$$i$$$辆卡车的描述。

## 输出

输出唯一的整数——使所有卡车都能到达目的地的最小可能油箱容量$$$V$$$。

## 提示

让我们详细看看这些查询：

- 第$$$1$$$辆卡车必须在不加油的情况下从$$$2$$$到达位置$$$7$$$，因此它需要容量至少为$$$50$$$的油箱。

- 第$$$2$$$辆卡车必须从$$$2$$$到达位置$$$17$$$，并且可以在任意城市加油（如果该城市位于起点和终点之间的路径上），因此它需要容量至少为$$$48$$$的油箱。

- 第$$$3$$$辆卡车必须从$$$10$$$到达位置$$$14$$$，中间没有城市，因此它需要容量至少为$$$52$$$的油箱。

- 第$$$4$$$辆卡车必须从$$$10$$$到达位置$$$17$$$，并且只能加油一次：最优做法是在第$$$5$$$个城市（位置$$$14$$$）加油，因此它需要容量至少为$$$40$$$的油箱。

- 第$$$5$$$辆卡车具有相同的描述，因此它也需要容量至少为$$$40$$$的油箱。

- 第$$$6$$$辆卡车必须从$$$2$$$到达位置$$$14$$$，并且可以加油两次：第一次在城市$$$2$$$或$$$3$$$，第二次在城市$$$4$$$，因此它需要容量至少为$$$55$$$的油箱。

# Digits Sequence Dividing

You are given a sequence $$$s$$$ consisting of $$$n$$$ digits from $$$1$$$ to $$$9$$$.

You have to divide it into at least two segments (segment — is a consecutive sequence of elements) (in other words, you have to place separators between some digits of the sequence) in such a way that each element belongs to exactly one segment and if the resulting division will be represented as an integer numbers sequence then each next element of this sequence will be strictly greater than the previous one.

More formally: if the resulting division of the sequence is $$$t_1, t_2, \dots, t_k$$$, where $$$k$$$ is the number of element in a division, then for each $$$i$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$k-1$$$ the condition $$$t_{i} \lt t_{i + 1}$$$ (using numerical comparing, it means that the integer representations of strings are compared) should be satisfied.

For example, if $$$s=654$$$ then you can divide it into parts $$$[6, 54]$$$ and it will be suitable division. But if you will divide it into parts $$$[65, 4]$$$ then it will be bad division because $$$65 \gt 4$$$. If $$$s=123$$$ then you can divide it into parts $$$[1, 23]$$$, $$$[1, 2, 3]$$$ but not into parts $$$[12, 3]$$$.

Your task is to find any suitable division for each of the $$$q$$$ independent queries.

## Input

The first line of the input contains one integer $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le q \le 300$$$) — the number of queries.

The first line of the $$$i$$$-th query contains one integer number $$$n_i$$$ ($$$2 \le n_i \le 300$$$) — the number of digits in the $$$i$$$-th query.

The second line of the $$$i$$$-th query contains one string $$$s_i$$$ of length $$$n_i$$$ consisting only of digits from $$$1$$$ to $$$9$$$.

## Output

If the sequence of digits in the $$$i$$$-th query cannot be divided into at least two parts in a way described in the problem statement, print the single line "`NO`" for this query.

Otherwise in the first line of the answer to this query print "`YES`", on the second line print $$$k_i$$$ — the number of parts in your division of the $$$i$$$-th query sequence and in the third line print $$$k_i$$$ strings $$$t_{i, 1}, t_{i, 2}, \dots, t_{i, k_i}$$$ — your division. Parts should be printed in order of the initial string digits. It means that if you write the parts one after another without changing their order then you'll get the string $$$s_i$$$.

See examples for better understanding.

# 数字序列划分

给定一个由 $$$n$$$ 个从 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$9$$$ 的数字组成的序列 $$$s$$$。

你需要将它划分为至少两个段（段——是连续的元素序列）（换句话说，你必须在序列的某些数字之间放置分隔符），使得每个元素恰好属于一个段，并且如果所得划分表示为整数序列，那么该序列中的每个下一个元素都将严格大于前一个元素。

更形式化地说：如果序列的所得划分为 $$$t_1, t_2, \dots, t_k$$$，其中 $$$k$$$ 是划分中的元素个数，那么对于从 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$k-1$$$ 的每个 $$$i$$$，都应满足条件 $$$t_{i} \lt t_{i + 1}$$$（使用数值比较，这意味着比较字符串的整数表示）。

例如，如果 $$$s=654$$$，那么你可以将其划分为部分 $$$[6, 54]$$$，这将是一个合适的划分。但如果你将其划分为部分 $$$[65, 4]$$$，那么这将是一个糟糕的划分，因为 $$$65 \gt 4$$$。如果 $$$s=123$$$，那么你可以将其划分为部分 $$$[1, 23]$$$、$$$[1, 2, 3]$$$，但不能划分为部分 $$$[12, 3]$$$。

你的任务是为 $$$q$$$ 个独立查询中的每一个找到任意一个合适的划分。

## 输入

输入的第一行包含一个整数 $$$q$$$（$$$1 \le q \le 300$$$）——查询的数量。

第 $$$i$$$ 个查询的第一行包含一个整数 $$$n_i$$$（$$$2 \le n_i \le 300$$$）——第 $$$i$$$ 个查询中的数字个数。

第 $$$i$$$ 个查询的第二行包含一个长度为 $$$n_i$$$ 的字符串 $$$s_i$$$，仅由从 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$9$$$ 的数字组成。

## 输出

如果第 $$$i$$$ 个查询中的数字序列无法按照题目描述的方式划分为至少两个部分，则为此查询输出一行“`NO`”。

否则，在此查询答案的第一行输出“`YES`”，在第二行输出 $$$k_i$$$——你对第 $$$i$$$ 个查询序列划分中的部分数，在第三行输出 $$$k_i$$$ 个字符串 $$$t_{i, 1}, t_{i, 2}, \dots, t_{i, k_i}$$$——你的划分。各部分应按初始字符串数字的顺序输出。这意味着如果你按顺序一个接一个地写出这些部分而不改变它们的顺序，那么你将得到字符串 $$$s_i$$$。

请参阅示例以更好地理解。

# Brutality

You are playing a new famous fighting game: Kortal Mombat XII. You have to perform a brutality on your opponent's character.

You are playing the game on the new generation console so your gamepad have $$$26$$$ buttons. Each button has a single lowercase Latin letter from '`a`' to '`z`' written on it. All the letters on buttons are pairwise distinct.

You are given a sequence of hits, the $$$i$$$-th hit deals $$$a_i$$$ units of damage to the opponent's character. To perform the $$$i$$$-th hit you have to press the button $$$s_i$$$ on your gamepad. Hits are numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$.

You know that if you press some button more than $$$k$$$ times in a row then it'll break. You cherish your gamepad and don't want to break any of its buttons.

To perform a brutality you have to land some of the hits of the given sequence. You are allowed to skip any of them, however changing the initial order of the sequence is prohibited. The total damage dealt is the sum of $$$a_i$$$ over all $$$i$$$ for the hits which weren't skipped.

Note that if you skip the hit then the counter of consecutive presses the button won't reset.

Your task is to skip some hits to deal the maximum possible total damage to the opponent's character and not break your gamepad buttons.

## Input

The first line of the input contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \le k \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of hits and the maximum number of times you can push the same button in a row.

The second line of the input contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$), where $$$a_i$$$ is the damage of the $$$i$$$-th hit.

The third line of the input contains the string $$$s$$$ consisting of exactly $$$n$$$ lowercase Latin letters — the sequence of hits (each character is the letter on the button you need to press to perform the corresponding hit).

## Output

Print one integer $$$dmg$$$ — the maximum possible damage to the opponent's character you can deal without breaking your gamepad buttons.

## Note

In the first example you can choose hits with numbers $$$[1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]$$$ with the total damage $$$1 + 16 + 18 + 7 + 2 + 10 = 54$$$.

In the second example you can choose all hits so the total damage is $$$2 + 4 + 1 + 3 + 1000 = 1010$$$.

In the third example you can choose all hits expect the third one so the total damage is $$$2 + 4 + 3 + 1000 = 1009$$$.

In the fourth example you can choose hits with numbers $$$[2, 3, 6, 8]$$$. Only this way you can reach the maximum total damage $$$15 + 2 + 8 + 16 = 41$$$.

In the fifth example you can choose only hits with numbers $$$[2, 4, 6]$$$ with the total damage $$$18 + 19 + 15 = 52$$$.

In the sixth example you can change either first hit or the second hit (it does not matter) with the total damage $$$10$$$.

# 暴力

你正在玩一款新的著名格斗游戏：Kortal Mombat XII。你必须对你的对手角色施展一次残忍终结。

你正在新一代主机上玩这个游戏，所以你的手柄有 $$$26$$$ 个按钮。每个按钮上都写着一个从 '`a`' 到 '`z`' 的单个小写拉丁字母。所有按钮上的字母两两不同。

给定一个命中序列，第 $$$i$$$ 次命中会对对手角色造成 $$$a_i$$$ 点伤害。要执行第 $$$i$$$ 次命中，你必须按下游戏手柄上的按钮 $$$s_i$$$。命中编号从 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$n$$$。

你知道，如果连续按某个按钮超过 $$$k$$$ 次，它就会坏掉。你很爱惜你的游戏手柄，不想弄坏它的任何按钮。

要执行一次残暴打击，你必须命中给定序列中的一些攻击。你可以跳过其中任意攻击，但禁止改变序列的初始顺序。造成的总伤害是所有未跳过攻击的 $$$a_i$$$ 对 $$$i$$$ 的求和。

注意，如果跳过这次命中，那么连续按下按钮的计数器不会重置。

你的任务是跳过一些命中，以对对手的角色造成尽可能最大的总伤害，同时不弄坏你的游戏手柄按键。

## 输入

输入的第一行包含两个整数 $$$n$$$ 和 $$$k$$$（$$$1 \le k \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$）——命中次数，以及你连续按下同一个按钮的最大次数。

输入的第二行包含 $$$n$$$ 个整数 $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$（$$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$），其中 $$$a_i$$$ 是第 $$$i$$$ 次攻击的伤害。

输入第三行包含由恰好 $$$n$$$ 个小写拉丁字母组成的字符串 $$$s$$$——击打序列（每个字符是执行对应击打所需按下的按钮上的字母）。

## ## 题目描述

给定一个长度为 \(2n\) 的数组 \(a\)，其中 \(1\) 到 \(n\) 每个整数恰好出现两次。

你需要执行以下操作恰好 \(n\) 次：

- 选择两个整数 \(i\) 和 \(j\)（\(1 \le i < j \le 2n\)），满足 \(a_i = a_j\)，然后从数组 \(a\) 中删除 \(a_i\) 和 \(a_j\)。删除后，剩余元素会保持原顺序拼接在一起。

设 \(b_1, b_2, \dots, b_{2n}\) 为操作前的数组。对于第 \(k\) 次操作（\(1 \le k \le n\)），设 \(x_k\) 为被删除的两个元素中较小的下标，\(y_k\) 为较大的下标。形式化地，如果删除的是 \(b_i\) 和 \(b_j\)（\(i < j\)），则 \(x_k = i\)，\(y_k = j\)。

设 \(S = \sum_{k=1}^n (y_k - x_k - 1)\)。求 \(S\) 的最大可能值。

## 输入

输入的第一行包含一个整数 \(n\)（\(1 \le n \le 100\)）。

第二行包含 \(2n\) 个整数 \(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{2n}\)（\(1 \le a_i \le n\)）。保证 \(1\) 到 \(n\) 每个整数恰好出现两次。

## 输出

输出一个整数，表示 \(S\) 的最大可能值。

## 样例

### 样例输入 1

```
3
1 2 3 1 2 3
```

### 样例输出 1

```
4
```

### 样例输入 2

```
1
1 1
```

### 样例输出 2

```
0
```

### 样例输入 3

```
2
1 2 2 1
```

### 样例输出 3

```
2
```

## 样例解释

在第一个样例中，一种最优操作序列如下：

- 删除 \(a_1\) 和 \(a_4\)（值 \(1\)）。此时 \(x_1 = 1\)，\(y_1 = 4\)，贡献为 \(4 - 1 - 1 = 2\)。剩余数组为 \([2, 3, 2, 3]\)。
- 删除 \(a_1\) 和 \(a_3\)（值 \(2\)）。此时 \(x_2 = 1\)，\(y_2 = 3\)，贡献为 \(3 - 1 - 1 = 1\)。剩余数组为 \([3, 3]\)。
- 删除 \(a_1\) 和 \(a_2\)（值 \(3\)）。此时 \(x_3 = 1\)，\(y_3 = 2\)，贡献为 \(2 - 1 - 1 = 0\)。剩余数组为空。

总贡献为 \(2 + 1 + 0 = 3\)。然而，可以证明最大值为 \(4\)。

在第二个样例中，唯一一次操作删除 \(a_1\) 和 \(a_2\)，贡献为 \(2 - 1 - 1 = 0\)。

在第三个样例中，一种最优操作序列如下：

- 删除 \(a_2\) 和 \(a_3\)（值 \(2\)）。此时 \(x_1 = 2\)，\(y_1 = 3\)，贡献为 \(3 - 2 - 1 = 0\)。剩余数组为 \([1, 1]\)。
- 删除 \(a_1\) 和 \(a_2\)（值 \(1\)）。此时 \(x_2 = 1\)，\(y_2 = 2\)，贡献为 \(2 - 1 - 1 = 0\)。剩余数组为空。

总贡献为 \(0\)。然而，可以证明最大值为 \(2\)。

## 限制

- \(1 \le n \le 100\)
- \(1 \le a_i \le n\)
- \(1\) 到 \(n\) 每个整数在 \(a\) 中恰好出现两次。

输出一个整数 $$$dmg$$$——在不损坏游戏手柄按键的情况下，你能对对手角色造成的最大可能伤害。

## 注意

在第一个示例中，你可以选择编号为 $$$[1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]$$$ 的命中，总伤害为 $$$1 + 16 + 18 + 7 + 2 + 10 = 54$$$。

在第二个例子中，你可以选择所有命中，因此总伤害为 $$$2 + 4 + 1 + 3 + 1000 = 1010$$$。

在第三个示例中，你可以选择除第三个之外的所有命中，因此总伤害为 $$$2 + 4 + 3 + 1000 = 1009$$$。

在第四个示例中，你可以选择编号为 $$$[2, 3, 6, 8]$$$ 的命中。只有这种方式才能达到最大总伤害 $$$15 + 2 + 8 + 16 = 41$$$。

在第五个示例中，你只能选择编号为 $$$[2, 4, 6]$$$ 的命中，总伤害为 $$$18 + 19 + 15 = 52$$$。

在第六个示例中，你可以改变第一次命中或第二次命中（无所谓），总伤害为 $$$10$$$。

# Vasya and Endless Credits

Vasya wants to buy himself a nice new car. Unfortunately, he lacks some money. Currently he has exactly `0` burles.

However, the local bank has $$$n$$$ credit offers. Each offer can be described with three numbers $$$a_i$$$, $$$b_i$$$ and $$$k_i$$$. Offers are numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. If Vasya takes the $$$i$$$-th offer, then the bank gives him $$$a_i$$$ burles at the beginning of the month and then Vasya pays bank $$$b_i$$$ burles at the end of each month for the next $$$k_i$$$ months (including the month he activated the offer). Vasya can take the offers any order he wants.

Each month Vasya can take no more than one credit offer. Also each credit offer can not be used more than once. Several credits can be active at the same time. It implies that Vasya pays bank the sum of $$$b_i$$$ over all the $$$i$$$ of active credits at the end of each month.

Vasya wants to buy a car in the middle of some month. He just takes all the money he currently has and buys the car of that exact price.

Vasya don't really care what he'll have to pay the bank back after he buys a car. He just goes out of the country on his car so that the bank can't find him anymore.

What is the maximum price that car can have?

## Input

The first line contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 500$$$) — the number of credit offers.

Each of the next $$$n$$$ lines contains three integers $$$a_i$$$, $$$b_i$$$ and $$$k_i$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i, b_i, k_i \le 10^9$$$).

## Output

Print one integer — the maximum price of the car.

## Note

In the first example, the following sequence of offers taken is optimal: `4` $$$\rightarrow$$$ `3`.

The amount of burles Vasya has changes the following way: `5` $$$\rightarrow$$$ `32` $$$\rightarrow$$$ `-86` $$$\rightarrow$$$ .... He takes the money he has in the middle of the second month (`32` burles) and buys the car.

The negative amount of money means that Vasya has to pay the bank that amount of burles.

In the second example, the following sequence of offers taken is optimal: `3` $$$\rightarrow$$$ `1` $$$\rightarrow$$$ `2`.

The amount of burles Vasya has changes the following way: `0` $$$\rightarrow$$$ `300` $$$\rightarrow$$$ `338` $$$\rightarrow$$$ `1337` $$$\rightarrow$$$ `236` $$$\rightarrow$$$ `-866` $$$\rightarrow$$$ ....
content.title: Vasya and Endless Credits

# Vasya 和无限信贷

Vasya 想给自己买一辆漂亮的新车。不幸的是，他缺一些钱。目前他恰好有 `0` 布勒。

然而，当地银行有 $$$n$$$ 个信贷方案。每个方案可以用三个数 $$$a_i$$$、$$$b_i$$$ 和 $$$k_i$$$ 来描述。方案编号从 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$n$$$。如果 Vasya 选择第 $$$i$$$ 个方案，那么银行会在月初给他 $$$a_i$$$ 布勒，然后 Vasya 在接下来的 $$$k_i$$$ 个月里每个月末向银行支付 $$$b_i$$$ 布勒（包括他激活该方案的那个月）。Vasya 可以按他想要的任意顺序选择方案。

每个月 Vasya 最多只能选择一个信贷方案。此外，每个信贷方案不能使用超过一次。多个信贷可以同时处于激活状态。这意味着 Vasya 在每个月底要向银行支付所有处于激活状态的信贷的 $$$b_i$$$ 之和，对应所有 $$$i$$$。

Vasya 想在某个月的月中买车。他只需拿出他当前拥有的所有钱，买下正好这个价格的车。

Vasya 并不真的在意他买车后还要向银行还多少钱。他只需开着他的车出国，这样银行就再也找不到他了。

这辆车可能的最大价格是多少？

## 输入

第一行包含一个整数 $$$n$$$（$$$1 \le n \le 500$$$）——信贷方案的数量。

接下来的 $$$n$$$ 行每行包含三个整数 $$$a_i$$$、$$$b_i$$$ 和 $$$k_i$$$（$$$1 \le a_i, b_i, k_i \le 10^9$$$）。

## 输出

输出一个整数——这辆车的最大价格。

## 说明

在第一个例子中，以下选择方案的顺序是最优的：`4` $$$\rightarrow$$$ `3`。

Vasya 拥有的布勒数量按以下方式变化：`5` $$$\rightarrow$$$ `32` $$$\rightarrow$$$ `-86` $$$\rightarrow$$$ …… 他在第二个月的月中拿走他拥有的钱（`32` 布勒）并买下这辆车。

负数的钱数意味着 Vasya 必须向银行支付这个数量的布勒。
